title: Six-platform game and application discovery
summary: Review 27 roots: add fifteen game/application research and reconstruction projects; record twelve duplicates, deferrals or out-of-scope candidates.
notes: Root personally searched C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, Amstrad CPC and DOS game/application reversing and reconstruction. Reviewed 27 pinned repository roots: fifteen additions and twelve duplicate, out-of-scope or deferred candidates. No worker performed discovery. Existing 5219-project main snapshot was used for duplicate and lineage screening, including GEOS and Harrier Attack hosted at alternative URLs. No forced platform quota: weak Amiga restoration claims were not promoted merely to fill a slot. Native semantics, retained original memory layouts, partial subsystem emulation, emulator wrappers and unsupported visual remakes are distinguished. Original-game and derivative-parity tests are not conflated. Reads only: no upstream game, compiler, installer, patcher, emulator or networking service was executed. Embedded UTF-8 proofs are matched to pinned Git blobs and commits were independently fetched. Root catalogue validation uses historical local activity fixture; remote ingestion validates against current main. A failed Batman repository fetch is not counted as inspected.

henols-c64-games-readme-md.text:
# C64 games

Reverse-engineered C64 games. Each game has its own folder with its reference files, the knowledge, the rebuilt source, the test scenarios and the documentation. A reference file can be a commercial release, a crack or a snapshot.

| Game | |
|---|---|
| [Barbarian](barbarian/README.md) | Palace Software 1987, Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior. Four projects in one group folder: part 1 (Combat Practice) and part 2 (the story game), each in two builds. The fighters, the hit check, the computer opponent and the final stage with Drax and the princess. The pictures, the sprites and the music. A hit-check bug that reads the wrong memory, and a dead two-player mode in part 2. Commodore 128 code and a cartridge header in the program. Three cracks (Raw Deal Inc., Hotline with its trainer, Fairlight) build from sources that are byte-identical to the captures of the cracks. Nobody examined a Palace release. |
| [Blue Max](blue_max/README.md) | Synapse Software 1983, by Bob Polin, C64 version by Peter Adams. A biplane flies over a diagonally scrolling landscape. The pages cover the map rows and sections, the airfields with landing and service, and the enemy planes, flak and special targets. They also cover the target city, the rank screen and the tune player. The copy protection is in the values of the original loader, and the first-stage loader survives in the Bandit dump. Development leftovers: an old charset, debug routines with a monitor exit and a disabled invincibility toggle. Three cracks (anonymous, The Bandit, Derbyshire Ram with two trainers and a Synsoft title line) build from one byte-identical source. |
| [Boulder Dash](boulder_dash/README.md) | First Star Software 1984, by Peter Liepa with Chris Gray. Two builds, each with its own byte-identical source. v1 is the Micro Fun build (the Charsoft crack). v2 is the Statesoft build (an original tape, the Donald Duck & Co and Roan cracks). The cave scan and the elements, the cave data format, the double-buffered scrolling screen, the title, the demo and the tune. A disk check that no release calls, the symbol-table fragments of the developer and a scan stop at the magic wall. The Statesoft loading picture of the tape at the start. |
| [Bruce Lee](bruce_lee/README.md) | Datasoft 1984, by Ron J. Fortier. How the program works, from the cold start to the last room: rooms, actors, combat, graphics, sound and music. A source that is byte-identical to the SAEGER crack, and a loader without the crack. Three cracked releases (SAEGER, TBC, DC) compared byte by byte, each a build of the same source. Nobody examined a Datasoft release. The Datasoft title picture, restored from the TBC crack, at the start. A fault of the game stops it at some room changes. |
| [Falcon Patrol](falcon_patrol/README.md) | Virgin Games 1983, by Steve Lee. A two-way scrolling shoot'em-up with a jet that hovers and lands. The flight model, the enemy waves and the kill test, the landscape map, the radar and the title with its high-score table. Code at fixed addresses with old copies and dead routines, and a start-up hang in one start of six. Three cracks (T.Bombardieri, Derbyshire Ram with its trainer, RGR) build from one byte-identical source. |
| [Hover Bovver](hover_bovver/README.md) | Llamasoft 1983, by Jeff Minter. Gordon mows the lawns of his neighbours with a borrowed mower while the neighbour chases him and Rover the dog helps. The main loop, the actors and their modes, the 16 lawn layouts, the screens, the tune player with its NTSC note table. The memory of Minter's assembler and a source line of lawn 14 in the block, and a speed bug that keeps lawn 16 as slow as lawn 1. Three cracks (The Friendly Programmer, Kraksnax "US/Canadian edition", Hokuto Force with six trainers and a high-score saver) build from one byte-identical source. |
| [Koala Painter](koala_painter/README.md) | Koala Technologies 1983, by Audio Light: the paint program of the KoalaPad, not a game. Two builds of the same source, each with its own byte-identical source: v1 (the Mayday! release, from an original disk) and v2 (the TBC and MAM cracks of 1984). The KoalaPad input, the menu, the 16 tools, the script language that draws the menu, the Storage disk menu and the Koala picture file. The disk protection of each build, the symbol-table fragments of the developer and CP/M bytes in the title file. The Koala Technologies title picture at the start. |
| [The Way of the Exploding Fist](exploding_fist/README.md) | Melbourne House 1985, by Beam Software. Two versions of the game, each with its own byte-identical source: version I (releases 2010 and Shadow) and version II (SCC and Mr. Z). The development from version I to version II: a dead bull bonus round and sample player in version I that version II makes live, keyboard control, a high score table and corrections. The Melbourne House title picture and the speech sample of the original loading stage at the start. |

popesick-julius-caesar-readme-md.text:
# Julius Caesar (C64, 1989) – Reverse Engineering und Nachbau

* **[DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md)** – Designdokument: Dateiformat, Packer, Speicherkarte, vollständige Spielregeln mit Formeln,
  Daten der 30 Stämme, Eigenheiten des Originals.
* **tools/** – Analyse-Werkzeuge (nur Python 3, keine Abhängigkeiten): `python3 tools/reverse.py JULIUS-D.D64 analysis/`
* **analysis/** – Ausgaben der Analyse (entpackter Speicher, BASIC-Listing, Grafiken). Wird lokal von `tools/reverse.py` und `tools/scenes.py` erzeugt und ist nicht Teil des Repositorys.
* **remake/** – spielbarer Nachbau. Starten: `cd remake && python3 -m http.server 8137` und <http://localhost:8137> öffnen.
  Tests: `node remake/test.js`.

**Spielen:** <https://popesick.github.io/julius-caesar/>

Das Originalspiel gehört seinen Rechteinhabern; das Repository enthält keine Originaldaten. Der Nachbau verwendet nur Spielregeln und Zahlen (Fakten) aus der
Analyse; Code ist neu geschrieben. Die Bilder in `remake/assets/` wurden mit ChatGPT als photorealistische Neuinterpretationen
von Szenen des Originals erzeugt. Musik ist ein Platzhalter (`remake/music.js`).

marcellmajor-c64re-gameinfo-readme-md.text:
# C64 game reverse-engineering notes

Working notes and small tools from reverse-engineering Commodore 64 games with VICE (live memory and disassembly) and static disassembly. Addresses are hexadecimal. Findings are only as strong as the session that produced them; each game section says what was confirmed and what was left open.

## Games

### Boulder Dash

Confirmed from live VICE reads and `asm_dir/boulderdash_unique.asm` on 2026-09-26. Behaviour comes from reading code and one-off memory reads. It was not checked with breakpoints or by stepping.

The playfield is a 40×22 tile map at `$0850`–`$0BBF` (`address = $0850 + row*40 + col`). Game logic scans that whole map; the screen matrix is separate, at `$0C00`. Each tile ID has a handler in the table at `$5F68`. The scan pointer `$32`/`$33` starts at `$084F`, and handlers index neighbours with `($32),Y` (`$29` current, `$01` up, `$28` left, `$2A` right, `$51` down).

Tiles seen live: `$00` empty, `$01` dirt, `$02` wall, `$07` steel border (explosions never overwrite it), `$10` boulder, `$14` diamond, `$30`–`$33` butterfly, `$38` player, `$3A` amoeba. Fireflies are `$08`–`$0B` (handler `$7172`: explode on contact, else turn left, else straight, else turn right). Butterflies are the mirror of that at `$7245` and leave a diamond when they explode.

Amoeba (`$7368`): a count of 200 or more turns every amoeba tile into a boulder; `$8C = 0` (suffocated) turns them into diamonds. Growth uses `rnd & $9A` (`$7F` slow, `$0F` fast) and writes `$3B` onto empty or dirt. Suffocation is detected once per pass at `$813B`.

The two Python scripts rebuild caves the way cave-start does (`$8AB9`: record copy, random fill, steel border, object list) from a 64 KB memory dump. They do not need third-party packages. Cave graphics in the PNG script come from the dump (2×2 multicolour chars, charset at `$3000`).

```
python3 boulderdash_cave_render.py DUMP
python3 boulderdash_cave_render.py DUMP --cave 13 --level 1
python3 boulderdash_cave_render.py DUMP --all
python3 bouldrdash_cave_png.py DUMP
```

### Petch

A Pengo-style maze game. Enemies chase only some of the time. Diamond ice awards 800 points. Walking into a border wall with the kick action stuns enemies that are on that same edge.

**Enemy AI** (`petch_enemy_ai.txt`). Update is `$4880`, called from the main loop at `$1034`. Up to four enemies. A decision happens only when the sprite is grid-aligned. Chase frequency is `$0D7F`, set at level start to `(level * 8) + $20`. Each frame the jiffy-clock low byte is compared with that threshold: below it, the enemy seeks the player on one axis (X or Y, chosen from the clock high byte); otherwise it keeps its current direction (`$0D84`). There is no pathfinding. If the chosen cell is blocked, it coasts. From level 4, enemy state 2/3 may pass cracking ice (`$84`/`$86`/`$88`/`$8B`) that state 1 cannot. Per-frame chase chance is about 16% on level 1 and about 38% on level 8; past about level 20 the 8-bit threshold wraps.

**Diamond destruction** (`petch_diamond_destruction.txt`). Clearing a normal ice block at `$39FA` always falls into `$6040`, which matches the erased screen pointer against four diamond slots (`$0D00`–`$0D03` low, `$0D04`–`$0D07` high minus `$D4`). A hit with `$0D10,X` still alive arms the animation at `$5E0D`. The per-frame machine at `$42CB` cycles sprite 5 (`$3A` → `$3B` → `$8F` → `$DF`) and on the last step calls `$439F`, which adds `8 * 100 = 800` via `$5300`.

**Freeze on wall** (`petch_freeze_on_wall.txt`). `$1E00` tests the facing tile for wall char `$88` (and `$82`/`$86`) and jumps to a per-direction stun routine: up `$5800`, down `$5837`, left `$586E`, right `$58AD`. Those mark an enemy state `$09` and a 48-frame timer at `$0DB8,X` only if that enemy sprite is on the same screen edge. Upstream, `$1903` uses bit 4 of `$0FFF` to split kick (wall stun) from a normal push. The notes did not find the call into `$1903`, so whether that gate runs in this build was left for a breakpoint on `$5800`–`$58FF`.

`petch_sample_report.md` is an earlier agent transcript (2026-05-16) about the red-ice animation and the 800-point award. Its own critic marked the score path as unproven. The diamond note above is the later trace that locates `$439F`.

### Vultures

Early C64 shooter (player at the bottom, enemies at the top). Code sits in RAM at `$0073`–`$20ED`. Analysis is from OGhidra sessions (gemma4 and grok-4). Where they disagreed, the grok-4 reading was kept: lives are zero-page `$8B` (init 3), not sprite register `$D009`, and `$0C7A` is score display math. There is no dedicated PRNG; enemy left/right uses the raster register `$D012`, and `$66` is only a sound-pitch counter.

Screen RAM is the enemy list. Sleeping enemies are 2×2 characters `$40`–`$43`. `$0D17` scans for `$40`, moves them, and counts them into `$3B`. `$3B == 0` is level clear (`$1148` increments `$8C`). The player bullet walks a pointer at `$57`/`$58`; a hit on `$42`/`$43` explodes the block to spaces and adds BCD score at `$53`–`$55`.

The vulture is sprite 4 (`$D008`/`$D009`), spawned by `$0E3F` and moved by `$0EDF` (signed directions `$5A` vertical, `$5B` horizontal). It drops sprite 5 when it lines up with the player. Sprite collision `$D01F` bit 4 kills the player: `$1052` animates, `$113E` decrements `$8B`, and zero lives restarts. The lives digit at `$04EC` shows reserve lives (`$8B - 1`), so 3 lives displays as `2`.

Sound is computed, not table-driven. `$1320` is a one-shot SID voice (pitch in A). `$1392` sweeps voice 2 from `$66` every 3 frames. The IRQ vector stays at the KERNAL default `$EA31`. BASIC is switched off; KERNAL is used only for `GETIN` (`$FFE4`) and scan/IRQ setup (`$FF9F`).

The summary also describes a title-screen viewer (`vultures_viewer.py`) and a charset dump. That viewer is not in this folder. A later note in the same file says a title-screen dump had hardware sprites off (`$D015 = 0`) and the bird drawn as charset characters; the routine list above still describes the in-game sprite path.

### Bubble Bobble

Level layout and the draw pipeline, recovered with the VICE debugger in April 2026. The notes file header still says "C65 Game"; the game is Bubble Bobble. Per-level tables are read from `$FF30` and `$FF94` in a 64 KB dump.

Layout bits are packed at `$C5F2`, one bit per column, back to back:

| Kind | `$FF94` bit 7 | Size | Layout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full | clear | 92 bytes (`$5C`) | 23 data rows × 4 bytes, right half stored |
| Compact | set | 46 bytes (`$2E`) | 23 data rows × 2 bytes, right half is a bit-reverse mirror |

`$FF94` bits 0–6 also pick the draw path: below 100 uses a nibble tilemap at `$0400` (path A, `$E3D9`); 100 and above uses the `$8B00` bitmask (path B, `$E000`). Decoded form is 25×32 bits at `$8B00`–`$8B63` (top and bottom borders from `$C58E`, left wall forced with `ORA #$C0`). Screen buffer 2 (`$5400`–`$57FF`) is the active display. Buffer 1 (`$5000`–`$53FF`) is a live snapshot, not a ROM picture. A second pass at `$E189` draws interior geometry from a variable-length command table at `$B695`.

Both scripts take a 65536-byte dump. `bubblebobble_print_levels.py` prints hex and a `*`/` ` grid (the `__main__` block is hard-wired to level 13). `bubblebobble_print_levels_2.py` mirrors compact levels with the same bit-reverse as `$E337` and prints levels 36–44 unless a level number is passed.

```
python3 bubblebobble_print_levels.py DUMP
python3 bubblebobble_print_levels_2.py DUMP [level]
```

### Captain Blood

Validated reference from 2026-09-27 for the RAM image `memdump_dir/landed_blood.bin`: the ship is on planet 0 and alien file 0 is loaded. The file tags each claim as code, executed in an isolated 6502 emulator, inferred gameplay, a story reading, or still open. The probes reproduced the file-0 decoder, all 187 pattern matches, both passwords, and all four coordinate replies. A read-only VICE check of `$4C00`–`$4DFF` matched the image. They did not emulate interrupts or a full playthrough, and only alien file 0 is decoded.

In that conversation screen, `$01 = $35` (BASIC and KERNAL banked out, I/O visible), the VIC bank is `$C000`, the screen matrix is `$C000`, and the bitmap is `$E000`. Sixty-four planet entries keep home coordinates at `$0600`/`$0640` and current coordinates at `$0680`/`$06C0`. Y bit 7 is a visited or departure marker; rendering masks it with `$7F`. Game flags are a bitset at `$9210` (`address = $9210 + floor(n/8)`, mask `1 << (n mod 8)`). The loaded alien file starts at `$6100`. File 0's script is `$621C`–`$67A0` and ends with `$FF`. Vocabulary strings, IDs 0–122, are at `$9418`. The player's eight icons are at `$5C80` (drawn on the right); the alien reply icons are at `$5C90` (drawn on the left).

Speech is pictogram words. A mouth click (`$4948`; screen hotspot x=144..175, y=107..126) walks the script from the start on a new phrase (`$E5 = 0`) or resumes the same phrase when `$E5` is nonzero. A useful line is often several mouth clicks after the phrase that triggered it. Record types in file 0 are PATTERN (`$00`), ACTION (`$40`), and CONDITION (`$80`). A COORDINATE token `[3,a,b]` prints a home position when `a` is nonzero (`$0600`/`$0640`, index `a-1`) and a current position otherwise. All four tokens in file 0 use home positions.

File 0 serves planet indices 0–3. Small Yoko (index 0, called BOW-BOW) accepts BLOOD, then a help trigger such as PLANET. Away from home he reveals home index 12, (140, 33) in this save. The planet-1 claimant's password is RENDEZ-VOUS 6 7, which reveals duplicate home index 60. Maxon's last stage accepts YOKO NOT DEAD IDEA 3 4 9 and reveals home indices 1 and 61. The ship-menu path `$0A76` calls removal at `$47E5`; alien index 60 or 61 in `$EA` increments `$FD`, and `$FD = 2` enters the end sequence at `$0A94`. Transport button sequences and the other alien files are still open. The planet-12 clue leads to file 3, which this reference does not contain.

Later notes (2026-10-09) cover the tape alien files the reference left open. They are not a replacement for it: claims there are tagged `[V]` / `[I]` / `[?]`, and the disk `PA`–`PP` files are a different layout, so they were not used as a substitute.

`captain_blood_alien_files_format.md` is the storage and interpreter note for the running tape version. Alien file number is planet index >> 2 (`$DA`, set by `$4D99`); one file serves four planets, split inside the script by flags F1–F4. Tape descriptors at `$5120` load banks `P1` and `P2` (and `B4`) at `$5C00`. `$0B1C` then scatters the 9400-byte bank into `$5A00`–`$5BFF`, `$8100`–`$8C3F`, and `$C700`–`$DFFF` (the last is RAM under I/O, so `landed_blood.bin` does not hold it; the bank was cut from `blood_run2_ram.bin`). The 13-entry index at `$584C` gives bank, page count, and virtual offset. `$0B71` copies the match to `$6100`. Files 1, 5, 8, and 12 are absent from the index, so those planets have no conversation (`$3E1E` falls through to `$3DCF`). A file is a header, a 3-plane operand bitmap, a script of PATTERN (`$00`) / ACTION (`$40`) / CONDITION (`$80`) records, and a compressed face unpacked by `$173D`. Take-aboard, put-down, and remove are `$47C1`, `$479F`, and `$47E5`. Removing planet 60 or 61 increments `$FD`; `$FD = 2` loads bank `P2` at `$0A94`. Only the five P1 files are decoded. P2 (files 6, 7, 9–11, 13, 14, and a second file 15) is not in RAM until that switch. `BLOOD CPT` at `$5120` is still unread.

`captain_blood_alien_files/00_index.md` is the shared conventions (planet names, presence flags `Pn+k`, encounter flags F1–F29, story flags from F420) and the P1 chain across the five decoded files. The per-file notes are walkthroughs of those scripts, with coordinates from games A and B:

- `alien_file_00.md` — planets 0–3: Small Yoko, No-No, Maxon. Same quests as the validated reference. An earlier file-0 write-up that called planets 60/61 a win is corrected here.
- `alien_file_02.md` — planets 8–11: Migrax (Great Bounty, Missile Brave). P10 and P11 are small talk only. One scientist answer points at P16, not Maxon.
- `alien_file_03.md` — planets 12–15: Croolis-Ulv (Dead Genetic, Great Destroy, Howdy Prison, Insult 4). The planet-12 snapshot `lamded planet 2.vsf` has this file at `$6100`.
- `alien_file_04.md` — planets 16–19: Croolis-Var (Good Nonsense, Male Warrior, Bad Crazy, Poor Genetic). These are the four planets file 3 asks to destroy.
- `alien_file_15.md` — planets 60–63: duplicates 1–4. Every message sets F5; `$47E5` then adds 60 minutes. Duplicate 1 gives P2-bank positions; after duplicates 2–4 are gone, P60 points at Torka on P27.

## Files

| File | Game | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boulderdash_memory_map_confirmed.txt` | Boulder Dash | Confirmed RAM map, tile handlers, zero page, amoeba and explosion rules. |
| `boulderdash_cave_render.py` | Boulder Dash | Console renderer. Live map at `$0850`, or rebuild caves 1–20 at a chosen difficulty from a 64 KB dump. |
| `bouldrdash_cave_png.py` | Boulder Dash | Same cave rebuild, written as PNGs (live map plus all 20 caves). Filename is missing the `e` in “boulder”. |
| `petch_enemy_ai.txt` | Petch | Probabilistic chase: threshold `$0D7F`, axis coin-flip, passability checks, coast fallback. |
| `petch_diamond_destruction.txt` | Petch | Ice clear → diamond-slot match at `$6040` → animation → +800 at `$439F`. |
| `petch_freeze_on_wall.txt` | Petch | Wall-kick stun at `$5800` / `$5837` / `$586E` / `$58AD`. Call into the `$1903` gate was not traced. |
| `petch_sample_report.md` | Petch | Agent report (May 2026) on the red-ice animation. Score award left open; see the diamond note. |
| `vultures_summary.txt` | Vultures | Memory map, loop, enemies, vulture, lives, and SID use. Includes the gemma4 / grok-4 disagreement. |
| `vultures_c64_disassembly.txt` | Vultures | Annotated disassembly of the same binary (`$0073` through the title screen). |
| `bubblebobble_level_data_notes.txt` | Bubble Bobble | 100-level format: `$C5F2` packing, `$8B00` decode, path A vs path B, subroutine list. |
| `bubblebobble_print_levels.py` | Bubble Bobble | Short dump tool: hex of one level plus an ASCII bitmask. |
| `bubblebobble_print_levels_2.py` | Bubble Bobble | Longer dump tool. The notes are embedded as a docstring, then a renderer that applies the mirror. |
| `captain_blood_validated_reference.txt` | Captain Blood | Validated memory map, conversation interpreter, and alien-file-0 quests and coordinate replies. |
| `captain_blood_alien_files_format.md` | Captain Blood | Tape-bank storage, `$584C` index, file layout, and the conversation interpreter. P2 and `BLOOD CPT` still open. |
| `captain_blood_alien_files/00_index.md` | Captain Blood | Coverage, flag conventions, planet names, and the P1 story chain across the decoded files. |
| `captain_blood_alien_files/alien_file_00.md` | Captain Blood | File 0 walkthrough: planets 0–3 (Small Yoko, No-No, Maxon). |
| `captain_blood_alien_files/alien_file_02.md` | Captain Blood | File 2 walkthrough: planets 8–11 (Migrax). P10 and P11 are small talk only. |
| `captain_blood_alien_files/alien_file_03.md` | Captain Blood | File 3 walkthrough: planets 12–15 (Croolis-Ulv). Loaded at `$6100` in the planet-12 snapshot. |
| `captain_blood_alien_files/alien_file_04.md` | Captain Blood | File 4 walkthrough: planets 16–19 (Croolis-Var). |
| `captain_blood_alien_files/alien_file_15.md` | Captain Blood | File 15 walkthrough: planets 60–63 (duplicates). F5 marks the +60 minute absorb. |

# Commodore C64 Game Source Code

## Purpose
- Start with an old Commodore C64 game disk which is as close to the original as possible (**g64** or **nib**).
- Include the copy protection.
- Produce a commented assembler listing which reassembles to an exact copy of the originaL binary.
- Make the source as variable as possible to allow any kind of modifications, data area and code relocation.
- Sometimes add some own ideas to the game soures code for fun and as a proof of concept.
- Sometimes add a (simple) level editor.

## Published so far
- **unmodified**
  - Loderunner                     https://github.com/Piddewitt/Loderunner
  - Championship Loderunner        https://github.com/Piddewitt/Championship_Loderunner
  - The Castles of Dr Creep        https://github.com/Piddewitt/The-Castles-of-Dr-Creep
- **modified**
  - Hansmanns Loderunner           https://github.com/Piddewitt/Hansmanns_Loderunner
  - Hansmanns Castles of Dr Creep  https://github.com/Piddewitt/Hansmanns-Castles-of-Dr-Creep

## Tools used
- Assembler: **64tass**
- Disassembler: **65xxDis**
- Disk manager: **DirMaster**
- Emulator: **WinVice**
- Converter: **NibTools**
  
## Project
- All content comes as a Notepad++ project

## Directory structure
- **dox** - _Additional documentation_
- **npp** - _Notepad++ modification instructions / language files / toolbar icons_
- **C64**
  - **tools**
    - **64tass**
    - **DisAsm**
  - **asm**
    - **Projects**
      - **file:** `npp_project_name.xml`
      - **Data**
        - **inc** - _C64 system includes_
        - **originals** - _Game sources_
          - **c64_game**
            - **asm** - _Source code_
            - **d64** - _C64 disk files_
            - **dis** - _Disassemblies_
            - **inc** - _Game includes_
            - **lst** - _Assembler listings_
            - **prg** - _Binaries_
            - **xtra** - _Additional files_
            - **file:** `all.bat` - _Call both, 64tass and 65xxdis_
            - **file:** `asm.bat` - _Call 64tass_
            - **file:** `dis.bat` - _Call 65xxdis_
        - **mods** - _Modified games_
          - **c64_game**
            - [same structure as above]

ytmytm-geossource-readme-txt.text:
GEOS KERNAL v2.0 - commented source code
by Maciej 'YTM/Alliance' Witkowiak
6-6-99



DESCRIPTION
This archive contains FULL source code of GEOS KERNAL v2.0. It is 99% identical to original OS. There are some differences in BOOTER code (I've removed installation code because GEOS from this package comes 'cracked' and 'installed'; there are also few changes in order of bytes in some places which is caused by using macros, it doesn't affect the system).



DISCLAIMER
This package comes from full disassembling of GEOS. I did it for my own pleasure and my own purposes in my spare time. It is meant for customizing the code and not for making big bucks ;). Anyway if you want it or not you may develop own versions of GEOS KERNAL only if you have the rest of OS - DeskTop, applications and so.



REQUIREMENTS
The only tool you need is a registered TASS package by MMS/TABOO. It may be obtained from: http://taboo.eu.org.
You may use other crossassembler (this might be too heavy task for C64 assemblers ;), but they have to allow:
- including files
- macros
- conditional assembly
- including binary files (or including series of .byte xx... created by converting binary file)
Then you have to change assembler ops: .byte, .word etc, macro definitions (in GEOSMAC.INC), and all macro statements in all *.TAS files.



INSTALLATION
To bring up a working copy of GEOS simply type from the DOS prompt:
GEOS.BAT
Ignore 'file not found' error - the batch file is trying to remove old kernal.
In few moments the file GEOS.PRG will be generated. Prepare your new boot disk by copying DESKTOP, auto-execs (CONFIGURE, etc.), input driver (if different than compiled), printer driver, preferences on a blank disk. Then move GEOS.PRG into that disk. From now on you can boot GEOS by loading that file and simply running it.
If you are using plain TASS.EXE you will get a file with load (and start) address of $5000. Ignore four warning messages.



CUSTOMIZING
Look at the file EQU.INC: you may change some values there.
This code is 99% identical to original. GEOS KERNAL optimized and ready for Ram-Cart and +60K RAM expansions will be available soon.


FILES:
Files are distingushed by their extensions:
*.BIN - binary files
*.INC - include files with constants and macros
*.TAS - source code files



THE SOURCES
Sources are organized in specific way. You can distinguish the code by few indicators.

1) Labels
All labels are identical to original geosSym and geosMac files. All OS_JUMPTAB functions are preceded with '_'. For example EnterDeskTop is placed in jumptab as:

EnterDeskTop		JMP _EnterDeskTop
(...)	big chunk of heavy code ;)
_EnterDeskTop			; code for handling this function

All other names are meant to descript the purpose of the subroutine. It was not always possible to name them in this way, so you may find some UNK_xx, xxxHelp_xx and batches of procedures with the same name but different number e.g. Font11, Font12 etc.
TASS does not allow local labels so all local labels have abbreviated subroutine name with a number on its end.

2) Indentation
Code is indented in this way:
		[tab2]				[tab6]
Label		LDA #$00			;$xxxx

Mnemonics are always placed on 2nd tab position and on 6th tab position you can find the current address. It is provided for all labels in the GEOS KERNAL.
Any code placed on the 1st tab position (instead of 2nd) would mean that the purpose of current/called subroutine/memory location seems to be unknown.



FILE LIST AND DESCRIPTION

sources:
BOOTER.TAS	- code for setting up kernal and boooting OS
DEPACK.TAS	- depacker code for PACK64 (part of TASS package)
DRV1541.TAS	- source code for 1541 disk driver
GEOS.TAS	- main file - contains includes for all other source and include files
ICONS.TAS	- part of lower kernal, majority of ICONS used in DialogBoxes
JOYDRV.TAS	- source code for joystick input driver
KERNALx.TAS	- GEOS KERNAL source code
LOKERNAL.TAS	- lower kernal code

include files:
CONST.INC	- part of geosSym - constant values
DISKDRV.INC	- needs to be included if you are including disk driver from binary file
EQU.INC 	- some constants, may be edited
GEOSMAC.INC	- the same as geosMac
GEOSSYM.INC	- rest of geosSym - memory locations
INPUTDRV.INC	- needs to be included if you are including input driver from binary file
KERNAL.INC	- some memory locations not described in geosSym
PACKOPT.INC	- options for PACK64
PRINTDRV.INC	- not included, contains jumptab locations for printer drivers

binary files:
[THEY DO NOT START WITH LOAD ADDRESS!!! IT IS PLAIN DATA]
BSWFONT.BIN	- generic font
PATTERNS.BIN	- 32 gfx patterns
UNKNOWN.BIN	- seems to be the rest of the BSWFONT file
DRV1571.BIN	- binary disk driver for 1571
DRV1581.BIN	- binary disk driver for 1581
MSE1531.BIN	- binary input driver for 1531 mouse
KOALAPAD.BIN	- binary input driver for KoalaPad (anyone saw that?)
LIGHTPEN.BIN	- binary input driver for lightpen
PCANALOG.BIN	- binary input driver for analog joystick (from PC) connected as paddles



COMMENTS
Well, the sources are not commented very much but the routines labels are very descriptive. You should obtain the GEOS Programmer's Reference Book (by Alexander Boyce) for full description for all jumptab routines and many GEOS structures. This document
is widely available on the Net in plain text or HTML format.



AUTHOR
Reverse-enginer I should say ;).
Maciej Witkowiak
ytm@friko.onet.pl



END WORDS
Have fun!

# Menace - Reverse Engineering & Modern Port

A project to reverse engineer the classic 1988 Amiga game **Menace** and port it to modern x86 hardware.

## Project Overview

**Menace** was a pioneering vertical-scrolling shoot-em-up developed by DMA Design (David Jones, who later created Lemmings and Grand Theft Auto) and published by Psygnosis in 1988 for the Amiga.

This project aims to:
1. Reverse engineer the original Amiga binary
2. Extract game assets (graphics, audio, level data)
3. Document game mechanics and behavior
4. Create a native x86 port using modern C++ and SDL2

## Project Structure

```
menace-re/
├── docs/              # Documentation and analysis
│   └── ANALYSIS.md    # Detailed reverse engineering analysis
├── tools/             # Analysis and extraction tools
│   ├── adf_analyzer.py
│   ├── disassemble_game.py
│   └── extract_graphics.py
├── extracted/         # Original ADF files
├── extracted_gfx/     # Extracted graphics assets
├── disassembly/       # Disassembled 68000 code
└── src/               # Modern C++ port source code
```

## Status

### Completed ✓
- [x] ADF file analysis
- [x] Bootblock disassembly
- [x] Hardware register identification
- [x] Graphics extraction (456 images extracted)
- [x] Project documentation

### In Progress ⏳
- [ ] Code analysis and documentation
- [ ] Game mechanic reverse engineering
- [ ] Modern C++ framework setup

### TODO 📋
- [ ] Audio sample extraction
- [ ] Level data extraction
- [ ] Full game logic implementation
- [ ] SDL2 rendering implementation
- [ ] Input handling
- [ ] Testing and gameplay refinement

## Technical Details

### Original Platform (Amiga)
- **CPU**: Motorola 68000 @ ~7 MHz
- **Graphics**: OCS chipset (planar bitmaps, 320x256, up to 32 colors)
- **Audio**: Paula (4-channel 8-bit PCM)
- **Storage**: 880KB floppy disk (custom format, no filesystem)

### Target Platform (Modern x86)
- **CPU**: x86-64
- **Graphics**: SDL2 + OpenGL
- **Audio**: SDL2_mixer
- **OS**: Linux/Windows/macOS

### Key Challenges
- **Planar to Chunky**: Converting Amiga planar graphics to modern format
- **Hardware Access**: Emulating Amiga custom chip behavior in software
- **Reverse Engineering**: Understanding game logic from 68000 assembly
- **Timing**: Matching original game feel without cycle-accurate emulation

## Building

### Prerequisites
- C++17 compiler (GCC/Clang/MSVC)
- CMake 3.15+
- SDL2 development libraries
- SDL2_image
- SDL2_mixer

### Build Instructions
```bash
# Install dependencies (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt-get install build-essential cmake libsdl2-dev libsdl2-image-dev libsdl2-mixer-dev

# Build
mkdir build && cd build
cmake ..
make

# Run
./menace
```

## Analysis Tools

### ADF Analyzer
Analyzes the structure of Amiga ADF disk images:
```bash
python3 tools/adf_analyzer.py extracted/Menace*.adf
```

### Disassembler
Disassembles 68000 code sections:
```bash
python3 tools/disassemble_game.py extracted/Menace*.adf
```

### Graphics Extractor
Extracts and converts graphics from the ADF:
```bash
python3 tools/extract_graphics.py extracted/Menace*.adf extracted_gfx/
```

## Resources

- [Original Game Info](https://www.mobygames.com/game/261/menace/)
- [DMA Design History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DMA_Design)
- [Amiga Hardware Manual](http://amigadev.elowar.com/)
- [68000 Programmer's Manual](http://www.easy68k.com/paulrsm/doc/trick68k.htm)

## Legal Notice

**Menace** is copyrighted software owned by Psygnosis/Sony Computer Entertainment.

This project is for **educational and preservation purposes only**. We do not distribute the original ROM or game assets. To use this project, you must own a legal copy of the original game.

Reverse engineering is performed under fair use for interoperability and education purposes.

## Credits

- **Original Game**: DMA Design / Psygnosis (1988)
- **Reverse Engineering**: This project
- **Tools**: Python, GNU Binutils, SDL2

## License

The reverse engineering tools and modern port code in this repository are released under the MIT License. This does NOT include the original game assets, which remain copyrighted by their respective owners.

hunkstalker-kult-atari-st-pc-port-readme.text:
# Kult: The Temple of Flying Saucers — Port a PC (Atari ST)

Port nativo (**Windows, Linux y macOS**) de **Kult** (Exxos/ERE, 1989), con
**español y catalán**.

![Kult Settings](assets/Kult%20Settings.png)

No parte de cero: el **C verificado** del Atari ST está importado en
`lib/kult-core/` y este repo añade un **backend de PC** (SDL3) para que ese mismo
C corra en Windows, Linux y macOS.

> **Estado:** el port es jugable de principio a fin en Windows y Linux. La
> versión **1.1.0** está publicada (2026-10-26) con macOS Universal 2 (Intel +
> Apple Silicon), firmado en modo ad-hoc y no notarizado. La **1.2.0** publicó
> el cursor a refresco nativo; la **1.2.1** (2026-10-26) corrige el ritmo del
> pixel-reveal y las transiciones de retratos. Incluye la ingesta de los discos
> originales, el selector de idioma,
> los packs español y catalán, guardado/carga y audio, además de **fullscreen
> nativo**, **F1**
> ventana/fullscreen, **F2** escala Estirar a pantalla/×1–×6/Auto y **F5/F6/F7** para
> ranuras de savestate (`saves/slot-N.save`), con avisos OSD en la **fuente original del
> juego**.
> El seguimiento técnico del desarrollo está en **`PROYECTO.md`**, **`TODO.md`** y
> **`RETOMAR.md`**.

## Core importado

El núcleo vive en **`lib/kult-core/`**, importado del repo
[`kult-atari-st-c`](https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c) mediante
`git subtree`. El build usa solo `lib/kult-core/src` e `include`; el resto de
documentación, tests y herramientas del core quedan disponibles pero no se
compilan.

Los cambios propios del port dentro del core están documentados en
[`docs/CORE_DELTA.md`](docs/CORE_DELTA.md). Al actualizar el core:

```sh
git subtree pull --prefix=lib/kult-core \
  https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c.git main --squash
```

## Documentación
- **`PROYECTO.md`** — contexto maestro, arquitectura y estado.
- **`TODO.md`** — tareas pendientes / en curso / completadas.
- **`RETOMAR.md`** — handoff de sesión (qué retomar y cómo).
- **`docs/REPOSITORIO.md`** — qué se versiona y qué queda fuera.
- **`AGENTS.md`** — reglas y arranque para agentes/colaboradores.
- **`docs/INDICE.md`** — índice de toda la documentación.
- **`docs/CORE_DELTA.md`** — core importado y cambios locales del port.
- **`docs/RELEASE.md`** — formato portable, contenedores y errores de release.
- **`docs/DATA_FORMAT.md`** — formato de `kult.data`/`language.data` e ingesta STX.
- **`docs/LANGUAGE_PACKS.md`** — packs español/catalán y limitaciones de fuente.
- **`docs/TESTS.md`** — inventario y política de tests.
- **`notes/`** — notas de sesión (histórico).

## Objetivo (resumen)
- Juego nativo en C, **sin emulador** (Musashi solo se usa como oráculo en las
  pruebas del core).
- Base **Atari ST**; el trabajo sobre Amiga queda para fases posteriores.
- **Español y catalán**, además de D/E/F.
- Backend **SDL3** (ventana, entrada, audio, GPU) + renderizador planar→RGB.

## Requisitos
- **Windows 10 o superior, 64 bits**, **Linux x86_64** o **macOS 11 o superior**
  (Intel o Apple Silicon) para los paquetes precompilados. Linux y macOS también
  se pueden compilar desde el código fuente.
  Release: <https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-pc-port/releases>.
- Una copia legal del juego con los dos discos en formato `.STX`:
  `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX`. Los nombres no importan; se identifican por
  SHA-256.

## Primera ejecución

El paquete no incluye el juego: necesitas `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX`. En la
primera ejecución se validan los discos, se genera `data/kult.data` y el juego
continúa arrancando en esa misma ejecución. **No hace falta ejecutarlo dos
veces.** En las siguientes ejecuciones, si existe `data/kult.data`, los `.STX`
ya no son necesarios y puedes borrarlos.

En Windows y Linux no uses una carpeta de solo lectura (`Program Files`,
`/opt`): el juego escribe `data/`, `saves/`, `kult.ini` y `kult.log` junto al
ejecutable o al AppImage. En macOS escribe en Application Support.

### Windows ZIP

1. Descomprime `kult-1.2.1-win64.zip` en una carpeta escribible.
2. Copia `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX` junto a `kult.exe` o dentro de `data/`.
3. Ejecuta `kult.exe` con doble clic.
4. La primera ejecución crea `data/` y `saves/`, ingiere los discos y genera
   `data/kult.data`; al terminar, el juego arranca.
5. Para volver a jugar, ejecuta de nuevo `kult.exe`. Si mueves el juego, mueve
   también `data/` y `saves/`.

### Linux TGZ

1. Descomprime `kult-1.2.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` en una carpeta escribible.
2. Copia los `.STX` junto a `kult` o dentro de `data/`.
3. Ejecuta el juego:

   ```sh
   ./kult
   ```

   Si falta el permiso de ejecución: `chmod +x kult`.

4. La primera ejecución ingiere los discos, genera `data/kult.data` y arranca
   el juego en el mismo proceso.
5. Para volver a jugar, ejecuta otra vez `./kult`; si mueves la carpeta, mueve
   `data/` y `saves/` con ella.

### Linux AppImage

1. Copia `kult-1.2.1-x86_64.AppImage` a una carpeta escribible y dale permiso:

   ```sh
   chmod +x kult-1.2.1-x86_64.AppImage
   ```

2. Copia los `.STX` junto al AppImage. También puedes ponerlos en `data/` si ya
   existe esa carpeta.
3. Ejecuta:

   ```sh
   ./kult-1.2.1-x86_64.AppImage
   ```

4. El AppImage es un único archivo: su contenido interno es de solo lectura y se
   monta temporalmente. Al arrancar, `AppRun` crea `data/` y `saves/` junto al
   AppImage, copia `language.data` y `LEEME.txt`, ingiere los discos y arranca el
   juego en esa misma ejecución.
5. Para volver a jugar, ejecuta el mismo AppImage. Si lo mueves de carpeta,
   mueve también `data/` y `saves/`.
6. Si el sistema no tiene FUSE:

   ```sh
   ./kult-1.2.1-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run
   ```

### macOS (Universal 2)

1. Descarga `kult-1.2.1-macos-universal.zip`, descomprímelo y abre el
   `kult-1.2.1-macos-universal.dmg` que contiene. Copia `Kult.app` a una carpeta
   normal, por ejemplo `Aplicaciones` o `Escritorio`.
2. Arranca `Kult.app` con doble clic. Si macOS avisa de que no está verificada,
   usa clic derecho > **Abrir** o **Ajustes del Sistema > Privacidad y
   seguridad > Abrir igualmente**. La build es ad-hoc, no está notarizada.
3. Si no hay `kult.data`, la app pide seleccionar `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX`.
   Selecciona los dos. Se copian a `~/Library/Application Support/Kult/data/`,
   se procesan y el juego arranca en esa misma ejecución.
4. Los datos y partidas quedan en `~/Library/Application Support/Kult/`. Las
   siguientes ejecuciones usan `data/kult.data` y no piden los STX.
5. **Desinstalar la app:** ciérrala y arrastra `Kult.app` a la Papelera. Los
   datos, ajustes y partidas de Application Support se conservan.
6. **Eliminación completa:** si quieres borrar también los datos y las partidas,
   haz antes copia de `saves/` y ejecuta:

   ```sh
   rm -rf "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Kult"
   ```

   Opcionalmente, si existe:

   ```sh
   rm -rf "$HOME/Library/Saved Application State/com.hunkstalker.kult.savedState"
   ```

## Controles
- **Ratón**: izquierdo/teclado = acción; derecho = acción + skip.
- **F1**: pantalla completa/ventana.
- **F2**: escala **Estirar a pantalla**, ×1–×6 o Auto; Estirar llena toda la salida.
- **F5**: muestra la ranura actual; otra pulsación mientras se ve el aviso cambia de ranura; **F6**: guarda; **F7**: carga.
- **F9/F11**: bajan/suben el volumen 10%; **F10**: silencia/restaura.
- **ESC**: cierra la ventana.
- Lista completa de atajos en `Kult Settings.txt`.

## Datos y diagnóstico
- Release **portable**: `data/` contiene los assets del usuario y `saves/` las
  escrituras del juego. En Windows y Linux TGZ viven junto al ejecutable; en el
  AppImage, junto al propio AppImage; en macOS, en
  `~/Library/Application Support/Kult/`. Las ranuras F5/F6/F7 van a
  `saves/slot-0.save`…`slot-9.save`; `kult.ini` recuerda pantalla, escala,
  ranura, volumen y silencio. La escala inicial por defecto es Estirar a
  pantalla.
- **`kult.log`** se escribe junto al ejecutable/AppImage o en Application
  Support en macOS, con timestamp. En macOS los errores fatales se muestran en
  un diálogo; en Windows/Linux van al log (salvo fallo del propio log).
  `kult-headless.exe` es solo una herramienta de desarrollo y no forma parte de
  la release.

## Origen y repos
- **`kult-atari-st-decomp`** — decomp ASM del ST, byte a byte (spec, no se toca).
- **`kult-atari-st-c`** — C verificado del ST, importado en `lib/kult-core/`.
- **`kult-atari-st-pc-port`** — este repo (el port).

Detalle en `PROYECTO.md`.

## Licencia
El código, las herramientas, la documentación y los packs de idioma del port se
distribuyen bajo licencia **MIT** (ver `LICENSE`). Los componentes de terceros
conservan sus licencias (ver `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` y `LICENSES/`).

Este repositorio no incluye el juego original. El usuario aporta su copia legal;
los assets del juego quedan **gitignored**.

matthieugros-fr-inertie-remake-readme-md.text:
# Inertie (Ubi Soft, 1987) : remake

Jeu d'origine : programmation Christophe Le Bouil, graphismes Patrick Daher, musique Xavier Talgorn.

## Jouer en ligne

https://matthieugros-fr.github.io/inertie-remake/

Le jeu d'origine n'est pas fourni : au premier lancement, la page demande les deux images disque d'Inertie
(fichiers `.dsk`, disquette 1 et disquette 2). Elles sont lues et gardées dans le navigateur, rien n'est envoyé.

## Lancer le jeu sur sa machine

Double-cliquer sur `lancer.command`. Ou, dans un terminal :

```bash
cd ~/inertie-remake && python3 tools/serve.py
```

puis ouvrir http://localhost:8642/

## Les deux modes

- **Original CPC** : le code Z80 du jeu de 1987 tourne tel quel dans une machine CPC simulée (`emu/`).
  Le comportement est celui de la vraie machine : physique, collisions, ennemis, menu, codes, sauvegarde des scores.
- **Amélioré** : même partie, rendu modernisé sur la carte graphique. Le pixel art est lissé par l'algorithme EPX,
  les couleurs vives rayonnent (lasers, réacteurs, explosions) et un éclairage suit le vaisseau. On passe d'un mode
  à l'autre en pleine partie.

- **Néo-Tokyo** : direction artistique inspirée d'Akira, sur le même gameplay. Le décor est redessiné par
  le code à partir de l'état du jeu (`app/state.js` lit la carte, le vaisseau, les textes et les pixels
  restants) : béton et chair biomécanique veinée de rouge, panneaux à katakana, survivants en combinaison
  blanche, vaisseau rouge Kaneda avec traînée lumineuse, explosion en dôme blanc, interface rouge et blanche.
  Les objets mobiles (soucoupes, comètes, boules de feu, tirs) sont repérés en interceptant les routines
  de dessin du jeu (&0FC2 pour les blocs, &0EEB pour les tirs) et redessinés avec une traînée lumineuse.
  Chaque planète prend la teinte de ses rochers d'origine. Les dialogues des cosmonautes deviennent des
  bulles de manga (réponse touche O ou N) ; les autres messages de l'écran de bord passent dans un panneau
  « transmission ».
  Effets d'image en WebGL (`app/neo_fx.js`) : halo, aberration chromatique, balayage, grain, parasites.

  Mise au point, dans la console du navigateur : `inertie.goto(planète, écran)` démarre une planète et y
  téléporte le vaisseau ; `inertie.frames(n)` fait avancer le jeu de n images.
  Les sons sont des effets générés avec ElevenLabs (`assets/sfx/`), déclenchés par les sons que le jeu
  original demande (`app/neo_audio.js`). Musiques Eleven Music (`assets/music/`) : Ruin Procession pour les
  menus, Tunnel Ritual en jeu, Collapse Loop quand l'énergie ou l'oxygène baissent, Victory Impact pour la
  victoire ; boucles calées avant le fondu final de chaque fichier, avec fondu enchaîné.
  Voix (`assets/voix/`, voix conçues avec ElevenLabs) : l'ordinateur de bord, voix de canard sarcastique
  (énergie basse, crash, refus d'un passager, game over), et le cosmonaute marseillais (demande, « oui »,
  « non », mort à bord). La musique baisse pendant qu'ils parlent. Explosion et tir refaits en qualité
  cinéma ; les anciennes versions sont dans `assets/sfx_pro/`.

- **Toutous** : même jeu, version chiens (`app/dog.js`, hérite du rendu Néo-Tokyo). Chiot dans une niche-fusée
  à petits nuages, chiens perdus en scaphandre, chats cosmiques, pelotes de laine, bouches d'incendie,
  aspirateurs ; os en guise de tirs, balles de tennis et onomatopées à chaque impact. Sons de chiens ElevenLabs
  (`assets/sfx_dog/`) joués très fort, aboiements-insultes façon « fuck you Tony » à intervalles réguliers.
  Création originale : aucun graphisme de Nintendo.

## Commandes

| Touche | En vol | À pied (cosmonaute) |
|---|---|---|
| ← → | tourner | marcher |
| ↑ | pousser | réacteur dorsal |
| X ou Maj | tirer | |
| Entrée | | rentrer (juste au-dessus du vaisseau) |
| Espace | posé sur une plateforme : sortir le cosmonaute | |
| O / N | | répondre à un savant |
| D, puis G + 1-4 | ordinateur de bord et guidage (posé) | |
| S / R | arrêter le guidage / revoir le radar | |

Après un crash, n'importe quelle touche relance le vaisseau. Manette : croix ou stick, bouton A = tir.
Règle (notice d'origine) : le vaisseau ne doit rien toucher. Les disquettes et les savants se ramassent à pied,
avec le cosmonaute, en surveillant l'oxygène ; l'énergie se recharge en survolant les réserves « E ».

Menu : `1` jeu, `2` table des scores, `3` redéfinition des touches. Le code d'une planète se valide tout seul au 6ᵉ caractère.

## Codes des planètes (relevés dans le jeu)

| # | Fichier | Code | Disquette |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | EJR | J12C58 | 1 |
| 2 | WTE | A35F13 | 1 |
| 3 | INV | J74V99 | 1 |
| 4 | ZBB | KIM742 | 1 |
| 5 | SHL | SUNC79 | 1 |
| 6 | FAX | G8I365 | 2 |
| 7 | CPA | RS232C | 2 |
| 8 | DUU | UBI57H | 2 |
| 9 | KED | O97P94 | 2 |
| 10 | YGQ | T78S26 | 2 |

Les plans complets des 10 planètes sont dans `ref/planetes/`.

## Organisation

```
index.html, app/      page, clavier/manette, rendu « Amélioré » (WebGL)
emu/z80.js            processeur Z80
emu/cpc.js            machine CPC : mémoire, Gate Array, écran, firmware simulé (clavier, son, disquette, événements)
emu/sound.js          gestionnaire de son du firmware et synthèse AY-3-8912
emu/original.js       chargement du jeu (reproduit ce que fait le chargeur LOD01)
tools/                extraction des disquettes, désassembleur, rendu des cartes, tests sans navigateur
ref/                  fichiers extraits de VOS disquettes, désassemblage, captures (à ne pas diffuser)
```

## Ce que l'analyse du jeu a établi

- Le jeu (`GAME.BIN`, chargé en &0400) est chiffré : octet XOR &AD puis + &12. Le chargeur `LOD01` le déchiffre, recopie
  50 octets de son propre code en &0FBB et en &B110 (protection : sans eux le jeu boucle), puis saute en &4012.
- Une planète est un fichier de 20 300 octets chargé en &5038 : une grille de 12 × 9 écrans, chaque écran faisant
  10 × 10 tuiles de 10 pixels sur 20 lignes ; puis la liste des cosmonautes (noms tirés au hasard) ; puis les graphismes
  des tuiles (100 octets chacune, en &7ACC + code × 100).
- Palette du jeu (table en &05AF) : 0, 1, 2, 4, 0, 11, 6, 15, 3, 24, 26, 9, 18, 20, 17, 13.
- Le vaisseau (8 orientations) et les explosions sont dans `HIBIN.BIN` (&A034). Sa position est en &041C (x en octets)
  et &041D (y en lignes) ; l'adresse écran de son sprite est en &040B.
- Touches par défaut (table en &21F1) : Z/X tourner, Maj réacteurs, Entrée tir ; joystick équivalent.

## Droits

Inertie © 1987 Ubi Soft. Aucun fichier du jeu original n'est inclus dans ce dépôt (dossier `ref/` exclu) :
chacun utilise les images de ses propres disquettes. Sons et musiques du remake générés avec ElevenLabs.

# Manic Miner (Amstrad CPC) – C# / MonoGame remake

Reverse-engineered from the CPC `.dsk` and the two `.sna` snapshots in `Amstrad Source Media/`.

## Projects
- `src/ManicMiner.Remake` – **the game engine used by the player and editor**: a clean C# implementation
  (typed fields, a `Willy` state object, guardian objects, coroutine-based program flow, a 16K CPC mode-1
  screen buffer). It does not use a Z80 memory image or the disk image at run time; graphics, tables and levels are
  loaded from `Assets/`. Physics, timing (300 Hz tick, 25 ticks per frame), collision and screen layout are
  translations of the original routines.
- `src/ManicMiner.Core` – the earlier literal port of the Z80 logic (runs on a 64K `byte[]`). Kept as a reference
  oracle for the parity test; it also supplies the shared `LevelData`, `CpcSound` and `Cpc` types.
- `src/ManicMiner.Game` – MonoGame (DesktopGL) player. `dotnet run --project src/ManicMiner.Game`.
  Optional: `--level file.json` (test one cavern), `--levels folder` (play a custom campaign).
  Keys follow the original (Q/E/T/U/O/@ or ← left; W/R/Y/I/P/[ or → right; Space/bottom row/↑ jump;
  Enter pause; A/S/D/F/G music; Esc to title).
- `src/ManicMiner.Editor` – cavern editor. Tiles, guardians (drag to move), Willy start, portal,
  palette/name/air/special-handler properties, F5 test-play inside the editor. Levels are saved as JSON in
  `~/Documents/ManicMinerLevels`.  The 20 originals can be edited and are saved as custom copies.
- `verify/ManicMiner.Verify` – headless checks (`dotnet run --project verify/ManicMiner.Verify -- . all|smoke|preview|parity`).
  `parity` runs Core and Remake side by side with identical random input and compares the rendered screen, palette and
  border every tick (title, scroller, demo mode, all 20 caverns; options `ONLY=menu|game|L|L<n>`, `TICKS=`, `KEYS=none`).
- `Assets/` – extracted data (`sprites.bin`, `tiles.bin`, `levels.json`, …) plus PNG sprite sheets/previews in
  `Assets/Sheets`, `Assets/Previews`. `tools/` holds the Python extractor/disassembler that produced them.

## Expansion packs
A pack is one `.mmpack` file (JSON: Name, Author, Description, Levels) holding any number of caverns.
- **Editor**: `Ctrl+G` marks/unmarks the current cavern for the pack (`[P]` in the title), `Ctrl+E` asks for a pack
  name and exports the marked caverns (or all custom caverns if none are marked) to `~/Documents/ManicMinerPacks/`.
  `Ctrl+I` imports the next pack found on disk as editable caverns, so a pack can be revised and re-exported.
- **Game**: packs in `~/Documents/ManicMinerPacks/` or a `Packs/` folder beside the game are listed in a
  "Select game" menu at start-up (Up/Down, Enter); `F9` returns to it. `--pack file.mmpack` plays one directly.
  Share a pack by copying the file. Caverns are played in order and loop back to the first after the last.

## Fidelity notes
- Screen RAM after the first frames of cavern 1 matches the snapshot byte-for-byte except for item flash phase
  (a frame-counter parity difference). The menu differs only in animation phase (Willy/piano keys).
- The CPC font is **not** in the supplied media; `font.bin` was taken from a CPC464 ROM image
  (`/usr/share/caprice32/rom/cpc464.rom`). Replace it with your own ROM dump if needed.
- Sound is a synthesised approximation of the AY chip/firmware envelopes, not a register-exact emulation.
- Busy-wait delays (game over, level-complete, pause) are converted to 300 Hz ticks by estimate.
- Special cavern logic (Eugene, Kong, Skylab, Solar Generator, Final Barrier) is ported but only smoke-tested.
- One deliberate deviation from the original: jumping no longer refuses to start when the cell under Willy's right
  foot is empty (the original made jumps near platform edges unreliable). Keys are also latched between the game's
  keyboard scans so short taps are not lost.
- Remake dependencies on Core are limited to `LevelData`, `CpcSound` and `Cpc` (data types, sound synthesis, palette).

## Tests

`dotnet test tests/ManicMiner.Tests` runs data, screen, pack, sound and gameplay tests, plus parity checks against the Core Z80 port. The GUI (editor and menus) is not covered.

meowmuhmuhcow-schicksalsklinge-readme-md.text:
# Die Schicksalsklinge – Quelltext im Attic-Stil

## 248 Fehler behoben – 34 Jahre nach Release

**Inoffizielle Bugfix-Fassung · spielbar ohne Compiler · das Original bleibt unangetastet · [gleich loslegen](#schnellstart-bugfix-fassung-spielen-ohne-compiler)**

> **Zum ersten Mal seit 1992:** Auf Landreisen trifft man **Höhlenbären und Kvillottern** und kann **Karene,
> Wildschweine, Auerochsen und Nashörner jagen**. Attic hatte das alles eingebaut, aber ein verkehrt herum
> geschriebener Vergleich machte es unerreichbar. Dazu: keine Spielhänger mehr bei Priester, Drache und Einbruch,
> keine 168.000 Dukaten mehr per ESC, und die Kvillotter beißt endlich. → [alle 248 Änderungen](BUGFIXES.md)

**Zusammen mit [Sternenschweif](https://github.com/MeowMuhMuhCow/sternenschweif): 473 Bugfixes für DSA 1 und DSA 2.**

**Das Schwarze Auge 1: Die Schicksalsklinge** (Attic, 1992), deutsche CD-Fassung 3.02, als lesbarer C-Quelltext.
Borland C++ 3.1 baut daraus eine `BLADEM.EXE`, die **Byte für Byte dem Original gleicht**
(MD5 `4ce035f95ead01a8b2553b4487544e5d`), **ohne Nachbearbeitung**.

> **Passt zur GOG-Fassung:** Grundlage ist die deutsche `SCHICKM.EXE` (CD-Version 3.02), wie sie in **„Realms of Arkania 1 - Blade of Destiny Classic“ bei GOG** enthalten ist (MD5 `4ce035f95ead01a8b2553b4487544e5d`). Andere Fassungen (Diskette, englisch, andere Patchstände) ergeben eine andere EXE. Vor dem Bauen die eigene EXE mit dieser Prüfsumme vergleichen.

*English: Source code of the 1992 DOS RPG "Realms of Arkania: Blade of Destiny" (German CD 3.02, as sold by GOG), based on the
Bright-Eyes project, reworked to plain C like the original. Rebuilds a byte-identical executable with Borland C++ 3.1. Includes an unofficial, untested
bug-fix build (~240 original bugs fixed, savegame compatible) behind compile-time switches.
Documentation is in German.*

## Schnellstart: Bugfix-Fassung spielen, ohne Compiler

**Alle Änderungen als übersichtliche Liste: [BUGFIXES.md](BUGFIXES.md).** Das fertige Paket zum Herunterladen gibt es unter **Releases** (rechts).

Für alle, die nur spielen wollen. Nötig sind Windows und Schicksalsklinge von GOG, sonst nichts: kein Python, kein Compiler.

1. Rechts unter **Releases** das Paket `…_Bugfix_1.0.zip` herunterladen (oder oben **Code → Download ZIP**) und irgendwohin entpacken.
2. **`PATCHEN.bat`** doppelklicken. Es findet den GOG-Spielordner (oder fragt danach), prüft per Prüfsumme, ob die
   eigene EXE genau die passende ist, und erzeugt daraus `Build\BLADEM_FIX_WICHTIG.EXE` und `Build\BLADEM_FIX_ALLES.EXE`.
   **Die Original-EXE wird nicht verändert**, das Spiel bleibt wie es ist.
3. **`BLADEM_FIX_WICHTIG_STARTEN.bat`** (wichtige Fehler) oder **`BLADEM_FIX_ALLES_STARTEN.bat`** (alle) doppelklicken.
   Das Spiel startet mit den GOG-Daten. Die Spielstände landen in eigenen Ordnern unter `Build\`, die echten bleiben unberührt.

**Funktionieren meine Spielstände weiter?** Ja. Die Bugfix-Fassung ändert das Speicherformat nicht, kein Feld, keine
Größe. Eure alten Spielstände aus dem GOG-Ordner erscheinen beim Laden automatisch und lassen sich weiterspielen.
Was ihr mit der Bugfix-Fassung neu speichert, landet in einem eigenen Ordner unter `Build\`. Eure Original-Spielstände
werden dabei nie überschrieben. Und weil das Format gleich bleibt, kann man jederzeit zurück zum Original.

Der Patch (`Patch\*.ndp`, je 35–60 KB) enthält nur die geänderten Bytes, kein Originalprogramm. Ohne gekauftes
Spiel lässt sich damit nichts anfangen.

## Danke

Dieses Projekt steht auf den Schultern von Menschen, die sich jahrelang, unbezahlt und aus reiner Liebe zu diesen
Spielen durch Maschinencode gearbeitet haben. **Ohne sie gäbe es das hier nicht.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Henne** | Er hat im Projekt **Bright-Eyes** die eigentliche Herkulesarbeit geleistet: Die Schicksalsklinge Funktion für Funktion aus dem Maschinencode in binäräquivalenten Code zurückgewonnen, dazu die Werkzeuge und den Weg, den historischen Borland-Compiler in DOSBox anzusteuern. Über viele Jahre, größtenteils allein, mit einem Stundenaufwand, der sich kaum ermessen lässt. Er hat den Rohdiamanten ausgegraben. |
| **siebenstreich** | hat Bright-Eyes weitergeführt, den C-Code geschliffen und das Projekt am Leben gehalten (github.com/siebenstreich/BrightEyes), und hat unsere Fragen geduldig und offen beantwortet. |
| **cmfrydos** | entschlüsselt mit dem **Riva HD Viewer** die Datenformate der Nordlandtrilogie (Dungeons, Ereigniszonen, Dialoge, Kampfsystem) und teilt seine Ergebnisse offen im Forum und im Wiki. |
| **Das Crystals-DSA-Forum** | Seit 2006 sammeln die Spielerinnen und Spieler dort Fehler, Beobachtungen und Rätsel der Nordlandtrilogie, im Thread „Bugs in Sternenschweif“, in den Truhenpatch-Threads, in Tipps-Sammlungen und in der Technischen Werkstatt. Viele Einträge unserer Fehlerlisten gehen auf ihre Meldungen zurück und sind dort zuerst beschrieben worden. Danke an alle, die dort über die Jahre geschrieben, gemessen und nachgespielt haben, und an die Forenbetreiber, die das alles erhalten. |
| **Alle Beteiligten an Bright-Eyes, am BrightEyes-Wiki und an den Reverse-Engineering-Projekten der Nordlandtrilogie** | für Karten, Datenformate, Dokumentation und den langen Atem. |
| **Attic Entertainment Software** | für diese Spiele. 30 Jahre später lohnt es sich immer noch, jeden Winkel davon zu verstehen. |

Fehler in diesem Repository sind unsere eigenen. Alles, was gut daran ist, beruht auf ihrer Vorarbeit.

## Grundlage: Bright-Eyes

Die eigentliche Pionierarbeit, das Spiel aus dem Maschinencode in binäräquivalenten Code zurückzugewinnen, hat
**Henne** über viele Jahre im Projekt Bright-Eyes geleistet; **siebenstreich** hat es weitergeführt
(github.com/siebenstreich/BrightEyes). Dieser Stand baut darauf auf.

| Neu gegenüber Bright-Eyes | |
|---|---|
| **100 % bytegleich** | die letzten Bytes gefunden: Stack-Segment gehört zu DGROUP, Link mit dem IDE-Linker (`BC.EXE /b`), der den EXE-Namen groß schreibt wie das Original |
| **C statt C++** | Attic hat DSA 1 als C übersetzt; alle 106 Module als `.c`, wie im Original |
| Assembler | seg008/009/010/013 in Attics Schreibweise, kommentiert |
| Beschriftung | sieben Prüfwellen, 117 Umbenennungen, Spieltexte als Kommentar an 3.406 Textstellen |
| Fehler im Original | 417 Einträge, davon 381 echte Fehler und 47 Exploits ([Fehlerliste](Analyse/Fehler/Spieler/Fehlerliste_Schicksalsklinge.pdf)) |
| 16 Fehler in Bright-Eyes | falsche Aufrufziele, Vorzeichen, Absturz in `pass_item` – korrigiert |
| Bau-Paket für Windows | `Bauen\BAUEN.bat`, Standard-DOSBox aus der GOG-Installation |

## Bugfix-Fassung: die Schicksalsklinge ohne die Fehler von 1992

Neben dem originalgetreuen Bau gibt es eine **inoffizielle Fehlerbehebung**: rund 240 Fehler aus dem Original lassen
sich per Schalter beheben.

| | |
|---|---|
| Stufe „wichtig“ | kritische und mittlere Fehler, darunter 23 von 25 kritischen: Spiel hängt bei Priester, fliehendem Drachen und Einbruch, Totenschiff beendet das Spiel für alle Gruppen, Absturz bei der Gruppensuche, Stufenanstieg per ESC bringt 168.000 Dukaten |
| Stufe „alles“ | zusätzlich viele kleine Fehler ohne große Spielwirkung |
| Neu erreichbar | Fix 181: Auf Landreisen sind erstmals Höhlenbär, Kvillotter und die Jagden (Karene, Wildschwein, Auerochse, Nashorn) erreichbar, im Original kam praktisch nur ein einziger Wildtierkampf vor (abschaltbar mit `-DFIX_0181=0`). Dazu behoben: Bär und Krakenmolch würfeln AT/PA verkehrt, die Kvillotter beißt nie, Krakenmolch-Endlosschleife (177–180) |
| Exploits | standardmäßig mit behoben (z. B. KK +5 durch Umlegen am Körper). Wer sie behalten will: `FIX_EXPLOITS 0` |
| Spielstände | **kompatibel**, das Speicherformat ist unverändert |
| Bauen | `Bauen\BAUEN.bat wichtig` oder `Bauen\BAUEN.bat alles` → `Build\BLADEM_FIX_WICHTIG.EXE` bzw. `BLADEM_FIX_ALLES.EXE` |
| Spielen | `BLADEM_FIX_WICHTIG_STARTEN.bat` bzw. `BLADEM_FIX_ALLES_STARTEN.bat` (eigene Spielstand-Ordner) |
| Stand | statisch vollständig geprüft, in DOSBox gestartet, **im Spiel ungetestet. Tester willkommen** – Prüfliste in [Analyse/Bericht_Fehler_Patches.md](Analyse/Bericht_Fehler_Patches.md) |

Welcher Fehler wie behoben ist und was bewusst nicht geändert wurde: [Bauen/FIXES.md](Bauen/FIXES.md).

## Bauen (Windows)

Ausführlich in [START_HIER.md](START_HIER.md):

1. Python 3 installieren.
2. Borland C++ 3.1 besorgen (z. B. https://archive.org/details/bcpp31) und nach `Compiler\` kopieren.
3. Die eigene `SCHICKM.EXE` aus der GOG-Installation nach `Original\` kopieren (nur zum Vergleich).
4. `Bauen\BAUEN.bat` → „BYTEGLEICH mit dem Original“ (unter einer Minute).
5. `BLADEM_STARTEN.bat` startet das Spiel mit der gebauten EXE und den GOG-Daten.

## Aufbau

| Ordner | Inhalt |
|---|---|
| `Quelle/` | 106 Module in C, Assembler, Miles-Klangbibliothek (`AIL/`), Header, Projekt der Entwicklungsumgebung |
| `Analyse/` | Fehlerliste, Namensliste, Kopierschutz-Bericht, Quelltextkarte, Beschriftungsprüfung, Spieltexte |
| `Bauen/` | Bau-Paket für Windows |
| `Werkzeuge/` | Werkzeuge der Bearbeitung |
| `Referenz/` | der unveränderte Bright-Eyes-Stand |

Lesereihenfolge: [LIESMICH.md](LIESMICH.md). Gesamtbericht: [ABSCHLUSSBERICHT.md](ABSCHLUSSBERICHT.md).
Fortsetzung: Sternenschweif (DSA 2) im selben Stil, vollständig rekonstruiert.

## Lizenz und Rechte

GPL v3 wie Bright-Eyes ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Rechte am Spiel bei den Rechteinhabern, kein Originalprogramm, keine
Spieldaten, kein Compiler im Repository: [RECHTE.md](RECHTE.md).

MooMoo mit Claude, Oktober 2026.
