# Captain Blood (C64) — Alien files: storage, structure and interpretation

Last updated 2026-10-09. Legend: [V] verified in code/data, [I] inferred, [?] open.
All addresses are for the running tape version of the game.

Sources:
- memdump_dir/landed_blood.bin ("game A"; matches live VICE RAM)
- sessions/captain_blood/dumps/blood_run2_ram.bin ("game B", extracted from a VICE
  snapshot; includes the RAM under I/O)
- the user's VICE snapshot "lamded planet 2.vsf" (file 3 loaded at planet 12)

Related:
- per-file descriptions: sessions/captain_blood/alien_files/ (00_index.md +
  alien_file_NN.md)
- raw decodes: sessions/captain_blood/alien_script_fileN_decoded.txt
- decoder: text_dir/captainblood/decode_alien_script.py

## 1. What an "alien file" is

Every planet has an index 0..63 (current planet = $DB). Planets are grouped by four:
alien file number = planet index >> 2 ($DA, set by the landing classifier $4D99).
One alien file therefore serves four planets. Inside the file, the script tells them
apart with flags F1..F4 = (planet index & 3) + 1.

A file holds everything that is specific to that group of aliens:
- a small header
- a bitmap with 3 metadata bits per script word
- the conversation script (bytecode)
- the compressed face graphics

The vocabulary (word table, icons) is shared and is not part of a file.

## 2. Where the files are stored

### 2.1 On tape: two data banks [V]

File descriptors at $5120-$5163 have this layout: 14-byte name, 1 byte ($02, or $09 for
"BLOOD CPT"), load address.

| Descriptor | Name | Load addr | Loaded by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $5131 | "B4" | $5C00 | $09F1 (new game) | alternative word tables (see 6.6) |
| $5142 | "P1" | $5C00 | $0A27 (new game) | alien bank, part 1 |
| $5153 | "P2" | $5C00 | $0A99 (mid-game) | alien bank, part 2 |
| $5120 | "BLOOD CPT" | $5C00 | [?] | [?] |

$0D36 is the load call:
- It writes the marker bytes $01 $23 at the load address and calls the loader at $085F.
- If the marker is still there afterwards, the load failed. It returns C=1 and the
  caller retries.

The disk release on the user's drive (/Users/marci/RevEng/C64/CaptainBlood/
CaptainBlood.d64, "IKARI" crack) is organised differently:
- 16 files PA-PP, each loaded at $6C00, one per alien file number
- the header layout is different
- none of the tape scripts appear in them byte for byte

It cannot be used as a substitute for the tape banks.

### 2.2 In RAM: a scattered "virtual bank" [V]

A loaded bank is 9400 bytes, $5C00-$80B7. $0B1C copies it into three free RAM areas,
listed as (start, end) pairs in the table at $5178:

| Segment | Size |
|---|---|
| $5A00-$5BFF | 512 |
| $8100-$8C3F | 2880 |
| $C700-$DFFF | 6400 (RAM under the I/O area) |

Together they form one continuous 9792-byte virtual address space: offset 0 = $5A00,
offset 512 = $8100, offset 3392 = $C700.

$0BFD waits for raster line $96, disables IRQs and sets $01=$30 (all RAM) for the
copy. $0C0A restores $01=$35.

$5C00-$7BFF is then free again and is reused as a work buffer. That is where the
active file and the conversation buffers live.

Reading a bank from a RAM image:
- Concatenate the three segments, then cut files out using the index (2.3).
- An image must contain the RAM under I/O for $D000-$DFFF. A VICE snapshot does;
  landed_blood.bin does not (it holds I/O registers there).

### 2.3 File index: table $584C [V]

13 entries of 4 bytes each: [id, pages, offset lo, offset hi].
- id bit 7 = bank (0 = P1, 1 = P2); id bits 0-6 = alien file number.
- pages = number of 256-byte pages to copy.
- offset = virtual-bank offset.

| Bank | File | Planets | Pages | Offset | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 0 | 0-3 | 10 | $0000 | decoded |
| P1 | 2 | 8-11 | 8 | $09CC | decoded |
| P1 | 3 | 12-15 | 9 | $119D | decoded |
| P1 | 4 | 16-19 | 6 | $19DE | decoded |
| P1 | 15 | 60-63 | 6 | $1EFA | decoded |
| P2 | 6 | 24-27 | 6 | $0000 | not in RAM yet |
| P2 | 7 | 28-31 | 5 | $05D2 | not in RAM yet |
| P2 | 9 | 36-39 | 7 | $0A63 | not in RAM yet |
| P2 | 10 | 40-43 | 3 | $10D5 | not in RAM yet |
| P2 | 13 | 52-55 | 4 | $1350 | not in RAM yet |
| P2 | 14 | 56-59 | 5 | $16D0 | not in RAM yet |
| P2 | 11 | 44-47 | 4 | $1B09 | not in RAM yet |
| P2 | 15 | 60-63 | 6 | $1E8D | not in RAM yet |

Files that are not in the index for the current bank (1, 5, 8, 12, and the other bank's
files) have no conversation: the lookup at $3E1E falls through to the "nobody here" path
$3DCF.

The copy is whole pages, so it can run past the end of a file. For example, file 0 is
2508 bytes, but 10 pages = 2560 bytes are copied. The extra bytes are never used.

### 2.4 Moving aliens, the time bonus and bank switching [V code, I meaning]

Three routines move an alien. All work on its per-planet flags (section 7):

- **$47C1, take aboard** (called at $41C9):
  - $E9 = 1 (alien aboard), $EA = $DB (which one)
  - $EB = F5 (set only by file 15, the duplicates)
  - clear its +2 flag (no longer at home)
- **$479F, put down** (called at $3DE6, from the "nobody here" screen with an alien
  aboard):
  - $E9 = 0
  - set +0 and +3 of $EA (present here)
  - move the alien's current coordinates ($0680/$06C0) to the ship's position
- **$47E5, remove** (called at $0A79, a ship-menu action, icon 1 -> $422F):
  - $E9 = 0
  - clear +0 and +3 of $EA (gone)
  - if $EB is set: $F6 = 1 and the time limit $EC/$ED grows by 60 minutes
  - [I] This is "absorbing" a duplicate for vital fluids.

Bank switching:
- $FC = current bank: 0 after "P1" is loaded ($0A33), 1 after "P2" is loaded ($0AA5).
- The lookup id = $DA, OR $80 if $FC != 0 ($3E06-$3E0F).
- After $47E5, if $EA is planet 60 or 61, $FD is incremented ($0A7C-$0A88).
- At $FD = 2, $0A94 loads "P2".
- So removing Duplicate 1 (P60) and Duplicate 2 (P61) switches the game to its second
  half.

### 2.5 The active copy: $6100 [V]

- $0B71 (A = pages, X/Y = virtual offset) walks the segment table to the offset.
- It then copies the pages to $6100 ($0BB5-$0BFA), crossing segment boundaries as needed.

## 3. Encounter sequence (load -> talk) [V]

1. $3DC3: conversation screen entry. Sets $E7 = 0.
2. $DA < 0 (no alien here):
   - If an alien is aboard ($E9), the player can put it down here: icon 0 -> $479F,
     then load continues at $3E06.
   - Otherwise wait for a click, then exit via $40A6.
3. $3DF6: alien present? Planet flags 100+5*$DB+0 and +3 must both be set ($4E7F tests).
   Otherwise go to $3DCF (nobody to talk to).
4. $3E06: look up the file in $584C. $3E2D: JSR $0B71 copies it to $6100.
5. $3E30: unpack the face. JSR $173D with X/Y = $6100 + word[$6104], destination $7400.
6. $3E48: JSR $4816, encounter init:
   - clear F1-F29
   - set F((DB&3)+1)
   - set F8 if this planet's home lead has the visited bit
   - $FB = 15
   - disable all icons
   - $4860-$4892: walk the script, enable every icon whose word occurs in any pattern,
     and clear every pattern's "used" bit
7. $3F4B: JSR $4934 (alien greets first). $3F4E: JSR $4370 (play the greeting).
8. $3F51-$4158: conversation loop.
   - A mouth click runs JSR $4948 ($40BF) and JSR $4370 ($40C2).
   - Each loop pass ends at $413A: if F6 is set, no alien is aboard, the conversation is
     still on and $E8 = 0, then $E8 = 1 and the teleport option is drawn
     (JSR $0FCA, X = $80).

Runtime confirmation: in "lamded planet 2.vsf" the ship is on planet 12 at (140,33)
($DB = 12), and file 3 (planet 12 >> 2) is at $6100.

## 4. File layout [V]

File 0 as the example:

| Offset | Address | Content |
|---|---|---|
| +$00 | $6100 | word: script offset ($011C -> $621C) |
| +$02 | $6102 | word: same value as +$04 in all five files [?] no reader found |
| +$04 | $6104 | word: face image offset ($06A2 -> $67A2) |
| +$06 | $6106 | $00 $00 in all five files [?] |
| +$08 | $6108-$621B | operand bitmap (276 bytes = 92 groups x 3 planes = exactly the 735 pattern operands) |
| +$11C | $621C-$67A1 | conversation script, 256 records + $FF end |
| +$6A2 | $67A2-~$6ACB | compressed face image |

All five P1 files, cut from the bank in game B, have the same layout:

| File | Planets | Size | Script | Face | Records (pat/act/cond/time) | Operands | Bitmap fits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0-3 | 2508 | +$011C | +$06A2 | 256 (187/39/30/0) | 735 | yes |
| 2 | 8-11 | 2001 | +$00C5 | +$046C | 149 (106/20/23/0) | 498 | yes |
| 3 | 12-15 | 2113 | +$00BF | +$04D3 | 174 (124/27/23/0) | 487 | yes |
| 4 | 16-19 | 1308 | +$006B | +$0288 | 93 (69/12/12/0) | 264 | yes |
| 15 | 60-63 | <= 1470 | +$0053 | +$0234 | 84 (59/16/7/2) | 200 | yes |

In every file:
- the script's $FF end is the byte right before the face image
- the bitmap exactly fills the gap between +$08 and the script

The bank copy and the working copy at $6100 differ only in "used" bits. The interpreter
writes flags back into the working copy only. File 0 in game A differs by one byte: the
greeting record $621C.

The P1 bank is byte-identical in games A and B (section 8).

### 4.1 Operand bitmap

- Pattern operand number j (counted in script order, only in pattern records; a 3-byte
  token counts as one) has three bits:
  - byte $6108 + 3*(j/8) + plane
  - mask = $80 >> (j & 7) (mask table $593B)
- Plane 0 set = REQ: the word must be in the player's message.
- Plane 1 set = silent: the word is NOT spoken in the reply.
- Plane 2 set = not a trigger.
- Reader: $4E99 / $4E9D / $4EA1 (plane 0 / 1 / 2), using the operand counter in $07/$08.

### 4.2 Face image

- 5-byte header:
  - word: offset of the bit-flag stream
  - word: offset of the run-flag stream
  - byte: cell count ($91 = 145 in file 0)
  - data bytes follow
- $173D sets up the streams and $1821 decodes them. A flag bit of 1 means "take the next
  byte", 0 means "repeat the previous one", using the bit masks at $50D5. This happens
  on two levels: the flag stream decides when to advance the run-flag stream, and the
  run-flag bytes decide when to advance the data stream.
- Output: cells x 8 bytes to $7400.
- [I] The face renderer then uses these cells (mosaic set-up $1B54).

## 5. Script format [V]

### 5.1 Records

Each record is:
- byte 0: bits 7-5 = type, bits 4-0 = operand byte count
- byte 1: flags
- the operands

A single $FF ends the script.

| Type | Name | Operands | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| $00 | pattern | words / 3-byte tokens | match $4B63, reply copy $4A18-$4A42 |
| $40 | action | signed flag words; none = "end encounter" | $4A85/$4A88 |
| $80 | condition | signed flag words | $4AC0 / $4AF1 |
| $A0 | time: clock > threshold | first operand = 16-bit minutes vs clock $C1:$C0; further operands = flag tests | $4AF8 (then $4B40) |
| $C0 | time: clock <= threshold | same layout | $4B0F (then $4B40) |

Time records occur only in file 15 (Duplicate 3, threshold 320 minutes).

### 5.2 Pattern flags

| Bit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $80 | used (set when matched) |
| $01 | repeatable |
| $08 | random skip, 1 in 8 |
| $04 | ordered match |
| $02 | always matches |

### 5.3 Condition flags

Directly consecutive condition records form one AND chain ($4AF1/$4B2E). When a chain
is evaluated:
- $05 starts at 0 ($4AC0). The flags of every condition in the chain are OR'ed into $05.
- On failure, the flags of the remaining conditions in the chain are OR'ed in as well
  ($4B51).

| Bit | Meaning when the chain fails ($4ACF-$4AEF) |
|---|---|
| $80 | barrier: stop the walk, no reply |
| $40 | skip ahead, evaluating only conditions that have $20 |
| $20 | marks a condition that still gets evaluated after a $40 skip (a block start) |
| none | skip ahead to the next condition and evaluate it |

Usage in the files:
- File 0 uses $60 block headers, $80 barriers and one $A0 terminal barrier (F999).
- File 2 uses one $40 (planet 8's section), one $20 block and one $80 barrier.
- Files 3, 4 and 15 use plain conditions, each naming its F1..F4 explicitly.

### 5.4 Action flags

$01 = run only once (then marked with $80). All actions in the five P1 files have flags
$00.

### 5.5 Operands

- Pattern operand byte 0 or >= 4: a word id, an index into the word table at $9418.
- Pattern operand byte 1..3: a 3-byte token [type, a, b]:
  - 1 HOUR: prints the 16-bit value a*256+b, or the current clock if both are 0.
  - 2 FREQUENCY: shows only the FREQUENCY icon; the value is not printed.
  - 3 COORDINATE: if a != 0, home of planet a-1 ($0600/$0640); else current position
    of planet b-1 ($0680/$06C0).
- Player messages cannot contain tokens. $4BFD drops word id 3 and keeps ids 1/2 as
  slots with leftover bytes. Patterns that need a COORDINATE token (such as the
  "ordered" identity records) can never be matched by the player.
- Flag operand: 2 bytes, high byte first.
  - Positive n = Fn set / set Fn.
  - Two's-complement negative = Fn clear / clear Fn ($4A67).
- Flag n lives at $9210 + n/8, bit (n & 7), mask table $5933. Routines: $4E57 clear,
  $4E70 set, $4E85 test.
- Per-planet variants: $4E1C indexes 100 + 5*Y + X. $4E51 clear, $4E6A set, $4E7F test.

## 6. Interpretation logic (routines)

### 6.1 Reader primitives

| Routine | Job |
|---|---|
| $4893 | rewind: $D8/$D9 = $6100 + word[$6100], $D6/$D7 = 0 |
| $48AB | read header: $06 = length, $04 = flags, A = type; Z/N set from the type; C=1 at $FF |
| $48D3 | step to the next operand (1 or 3 bytes); bumps the operand counter $07/$08 |
| $48EF | write the flags byte back (stores the "used" bit), advance $D8; for patterns also add the operand count to $D6 |
| $4AB8 | run all action records that directly follow |
| $4925 | scan the player's word list $5CA0 (skips 3-byte tokens) |
| $4A67 | decode a signed flag operand into X/Y |

### 6.2 Entry points

- $4934 greeting: empty word list ($5CA0 = $FF x 8), up to 8 attempts.
- $4948 mouth click:
  - $E5 = 0 (fresh message):
    - $4BFD converts the icons in $5C80 to word ids in $5CA0 through $9718. An empty
      message ends here.
    - $4331 / $434B clear and redraw the player row.
    - $4991 fresh start:
      - F7 is set when the $FB countdown (15 messages) runs out, or on a 1 in 16 chance.
      - F9 is set on a 1 in 4 chance (cleared otherwise).
      - Then $4893 rewind, $4AB8 leading actions (e.g. file 15's "set F5"), and the
        $49C1 walk.
  - $E5 != 0 (continuation): $49C1 resumes where the last walk stopped, with the same
    words. The player's new icons are not read yet.
  - Afterwards: if a reply was produced ($E6), $E5++. Otherwise $E5 = 0. Then $4C32.

### 6.3 The walk, $49C1

Records are read in order until one produces a reply.

- **Condition chain** ($4AC0 -> $4AF1): every operand must hold (flag tests, time tests).
  - Pass: the actions that follow the chain run ($4AB8) and the walk continues.
  - Fail: see 5.3.
- **Action** met during the walk without a match: skipped ($49D5 -> $48EF).
- **Pattern** ($4B63):
  - Reject if used and not repeatable.
  - Reject on the 1-in-8 random skip if $08 is set.
  - Reject if it has no operands.
  - $04 ordered: all words must appear in order.
  - $02 always: accept.
  - Otherwise: every REQ word must be present, and at least one REQ or TRIG word must
    be present.
- **On a match:**
  - $48EF marks the pattern used.
  - $4AB8 runs the following actions:
    - set/clear flags
    - an action with no operands sets $E7 = conversation over
    - $01 "once" actions are skipped if already used
  - $4A18-$4A42 copy every operand whose plane-1 bit is clear into $5CB0 (3-byte tokens
    kept whole).
  - If anything was copied: $FF-terminate, $E6++, stop. The stack is restored from $0B
    at $4BF9.
  - If nothing was copied (silent match): keep walking.

### 6.4 Output

- $4C32 builds the reply icons:
  - word id -> icon through the $5C00 map (built at $4851 from $9718)
  - HOUR / COORDINATE tokens -> digit icons ($4CBB -> $0F5D), with separator icon $6F
  - FREQUENCY tokens consume their bytes but print nothing
  - result in $5C90
- $4370 plays it, one icon per slot, with the beep $43BC.

### 6.5 Interpreter state (zero page)

| Address | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $D8/$D9 | record pointer |
| $D6/$D7 | operand counter |
| $06 | bytes left in the current record |
| $04 | current flags |
| $05 | condition-chain flags |
| $0B | saved stack pointer |
| $E5 | continuation pending |
| $E6 | reply produced |
| $E7 | conversation over |
| $E8 | teleport option shown |
| $0A | attempt count |

### 6.6 Shared vocabulary (not in the files)

- $9418-$9717 word table, 3 pages: 123 high-bit-terminated strings (ids 0-122), zero
  padded.
  - id 0 = blank; 1-3 = HOUR / FREQUENCY / COORDINATE; 111-120 = digits "0".."9".
- At new game, a byte saved on the stack at $09D1 ($FF) selects which word table to use
  ($09FB-$0A25):
  - '1' keeps the built-in table
  - '2' copies 3 pages from $5C00 (loaded "B4")
  - anything else copies from $5F00
  - [I] Probably the language choice.
- $9718: icon -> word id (bit 7 = icon disabled).
- $9798 / $9C58: icon graphics.

## 7. Flags the files use

### 7.1 Per encounter (F1-F29, cleared at $4816)

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| F1-F4 | which planet of the file [V] |
| F5 | set by file 15 on every message; $47C1 copies it to $EB, and $47E5 then adds 60 minutes [V]. [I] "This alien is a duplicate." |
| F6 | set by scripts right after "teleport" lines; makes the conversation loop offer the teleport ($413A-$4155) [V] |
| F7 | "talked long enough": 15 messages, a 1-in-16 chance per message, or set by a script. Many story speeches need it [V]. (Earlier notes called it "impatience".) |
| F8 | this planet's home lead is marked visited [V] |
| F9 | set on a 1 in 4 chance per message [V]. File 2 uses it as a random refusal. |
| F10-F29 | script scratch flags (answers given, topics raised) |

### 7.2 Per planet: F100 + 5n + k ("Pn+k"), saved

| k | Meaning | Changed by |
|---|---|---|
| +0 and +3 | alien present; both needed for a conversation ($3DF6) [V] | set: $479F; cleared: $47E5. Scripts also spawn (set +3) and remove (clear +0 or +3) aliens. |
| +2 | alien at its home coordinates (recomputed at $4DF8-$4E0B) [V] | cleared: $47C1 |
| +1 | [?] | cleared with +0 by $4D1C ([I] planet destruction) and by file 4's Bad Crazy |
| +4 | [?] copied to $DC on landing | |

At the start of both recorded games:
- P0, P2, P8-P19 and P60-P63 are present.
- P1 and P3 are absent (their +3 is clear) until Yoko's story sets it.
- P4-P7 are absent.

### 7.3 Story flags (F40 and up), saved

- F40-F49: set at new game; cleared one by one by the visit counter in $4D1C.
- Per file:

| File | Story flags |
|---|---|
| 0 | F420, F435, F436, F437 (F437 never set), F999 (never set, terminal barrier) |
| 2 | F460, F465, F466 |
| 3 | F480, F485, F487, F490 |
| 4 | F500 |
| 15 | F998 |

- Scripts also read and write other planets' Pn+k flags. This is how the stories link
  across files (see alien_files/00_index.md).

## 8. Script conventions found in the content [V data, I meaning]

- **Planet names.** Planets are named with word + digits. Known names: P0 BOW-BOW,
  P1 IDEA 3 4 9, P3 RENDEZ-VOUS 6 7, P8 REPRODUCTION 1 4, P9 REPRODUCTION 1 2 8,
  P12 TRAP 4, P13 GREAT TRAP, P14 BAD TRAP, P15 (INSULT) 8 0, P16 TRAP 2, P17 GREAT FEAR,
  P18 KILL YOU, P19 TRAP 1. The file-0 "passwords" are these names.
- **Identity records.** Each file has records that tie a character name, a COORDINATE
  token and a planet name together. Examples:
  - "MAXON RENDEZ-VOUS 6 7" (silent, file 0)
  - "GREAT BOUNTY <P8> REPRODUCTION 1 4" (file 2)
  - "DEAD GENETIC <P12> TRAP 4" (ordered, file 3)

  The ordered ones can never be matched by the player (5.5).
- **Character introductions.** Each character introduces itself with "ME <name>" and
  "PLANET (ME) = <planet name>", usually followed by its own COORDINATE.
- **Teleport offers.** "... TELEPORT ..." lines are followed by an action that sets F6.
- **Removal.** Story blocks test other planets' presence flags ("you killed X") and
  remove aliens by clearing +0 or +3.

## 9. What changes between games (run comparison) [V]

landed_blood.bin (game A, planet 0 at 145,69) was compared with blood_run2_ram.bin
(game B, planet 0 at 232,125). Both are at the start: $DB=0, $FC=0, $FD=0.

Identical in both:
- the whole P1 bank in all three segments (in game A, $D000-$DFFF could not be compared
  because the dump holds I/O registers there)
- the segment table $5178, the file index $584C, the tape descriptors
- the word table $9418, the icon table $9718
- every flag from F16 up, including all per-planet presence flags

Different:
- planet coordinates $0600-$06FF (254 of 256 bytes; random at new game, $46F5)
- ship position $E0/$E1, clock $C0
- per-encounter flags (F1-F15)
- face mosaic $54C2-$54D1 (random)
- self-modifying operands and the IRQ stage vector ($0F42, $0F4F, $1C1B, $1C3F, $36Ex,
  $4EE8, ...)
- the work buffer $5C00-$7BFF

So the alien files, and with them every script, planet name and story flag, are the
same in every game. COORDINATE tokens name planets by index, and the coordinates are
looked up in the per-game table at speaking time, so only the numbers differ.

## 10. Corrections to earlier notes

- $0A94 is the "P2" bank load, not an end/win sequence. Not yet fixed in:
  - memory_map_verified.md
  - conversation_coordinate_reveal.md
  - alien_script_file0_explained.md, section 7
  - captain_blood_validated_reference.txt ($FD / $0A94 lines)
- F7 is "talked long enough", not "impatience" (conversation_coordinate_reveal.md,
  memory_map_verified.md).
- The file-0 "passwords" RENDEZ-VOUS 6 7 and IDEA 3 4 9 are planet names (Maxon's and
  No-No's).
- The word table occupies $9418-$9717 (123 entries + zero padding). It does not end at
  $972C.
- Decoder fix (2026-10-09, text_dir/captainblood/decode_alien_script.py): in time
  records only the first operand is minutes; the rest are flags. The output for files
  without time records is unchanged.

## 11. Open

- The P2 files (6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15) need a RAM image taken after "P2" is loaded.
  Plan: restore a landed snapshot in VICE, attach CaptainBlood_tape.tap, make the game
  run $0A94, then snapshot.
- What the ship-menu action at $0A76 / $422F is called in the game (inferred: absorb /
  remove the alien aboard).
- What $6102 (always equal to the face offset), $6106 and the "BLOOD CPT" tape file are.
- Exactly how the unpacked face at $7400 is drawn.
- Duplicate 1 (file 15) gives "current" positions of planets 28, 36 and 24 for
  duplicates 2-4. This bank has duplicates 2-4 on 61-63. Lying, or bank-P2 positions?
- File 3 tests P12+2 where P13+2 seems intended ($64FD).
- $4D1C (clears +0/+1 at the ship's position; event 7 of the $19E5 loop) is assumed to
  be planet destruction; not confirmed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Extract and convert Amiga graphics from Menace
Amiga uses planar bitmap format - each bitplane is stored separately
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

# Common Amiga palette (can be overridden by game)
DEFAULT_PALETTE = [
    (0x00, 0x00, 0x00),  # 0: Black
    (0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF),  # 1: White  
    (0xFF, 0x00, 0x00),  # 2: Red
    (0x00, 0xFF, 0x00),  # 3: Green
    (0x00, 0x00, 0xFF),  # 4: Blue
    (0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00),  # 5: Yellow
    (0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF),  # 6: Magenta
    (0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF),  # 7: Cyan
    (0x80, 0x80, 0x80),  # 8: Gray
    (0xC0, 0xC0, 0xC0),  # 9: Light Gray
    (0x80, 0x00, 0x00),  # 10: Dark Red
    (0x00, 0x80, 0x00),  # 11: Dark Green
    (0x00, 0x00, 0x80),  # 12: Dark Blue
    (0x80, 0x80, 0x00),  # 13: Olive
    (0x80, 0x00, 0x80),  # 14: Purple
    (0x00, 0x80, 0x80),  # 15: Teal
]

def planar_to_chunky(planes, width, height):
    """
    Convert Amiga planar bitmap to chunky (standard) format
    planes: list of bitplane data (each is a 2D numpy array)
    Returns: 2D array of pixel values
    """
    num_planes = len(planes)
    pixels = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8)
    
    for plane_idx, plane in enumerate(planes):
        bit_value = 1 << plane_idx
        pixels |= (plane * bit_value)
    
    return pixels

def extract_bitplane(data, width, height, offset=0):
    """Extract a single bitplane from raw data"""
    bytes_per_row = width // 8
    plane_size = bytes_per_row * height
    
    if offset + plane_size > len(data):
        return None
    
    plane_data = data[offset:offset + plane_size]
    plane = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8)
    
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            byte_offset = y * bytes_per_row + x // 8
            bit_offset = 7 - (x % 8)
            
            if byte_offset < len(plane_data):
                byte_val = plane_data[byte_offset]
                bit_val = (byte_val >> bit_offset) & 1
                plane[y, x] = bit_val
    
    return plane

def try_extract_image(data, width, height, num_bitplanes, offset=0, palette=None):
    """Try to extract an image with given parameters"""
    if palette is None:
        palette = DEFAULT_PALETTE[:2**num_bitplanes]
    
    # Extract bitplanes
    planes = []
    plane_size = (width // 8) * height
    
    for i in range(num_bitplanes):
        plane_offset = offset + (i * plane_size)
        plane = extract_bitplane(data, width, height, plane_offset)
        if plane is None:
            return None
        planes.append(plane)
    
    # Convert to chunky format
    pixels = planar_to_chunky(planes, width, height)
    
    # Create PIL image
    img = Image.new('RGB', (width, height))
    img_pixels = img.load()
    
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            color_idx = pixels[y, x]
            if color_idx < len(palette):
                img_pixels[x, y] = palette[color_idx]
            else:
                img_pixels[x, y] = (255, 0, 255)  # Magenta for out of range
    
    return img

def scan_for_graphics(adf_file, output_dir):
    """Scan the ADF for likely graphics data"""
    with open(adf_file, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()
    
    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    # Common Amiga screen dimensions
    configs = [
        # (width, height, bitplanes, description)
        (320, 200, 4, 'Standard Low-Res 16 colors'),
        (320, 256, 4, 'PAL Low-Res 16 colors'),
        (320, 200, 5, 'Standard Low-Res 32 colors'),
        (320, 256, 5, 'PAL Low-Res 32 colors'),
        (640, 200, 4, 'Hi-Res 16 colors'),
        (160, 200, 4, 'Low-Res sprites'),
        (16, 16, 4, 'Small sprites'),
        (32, 32, 4, 'Medium sprites'),
        (48, 48, 4, 'Large sprites'),
    ]
    
    print(f"Scanning {adf_file.name} for graphics...")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    found_count = 0
    
    # Scan at various offsets
    scan_offsets = list(range(0, len(data), 8192))  # Every 8KB
    
    for width, height, bitplanes, desc in configs:
        total_size = (width // 8) * height * bitplanes
        
        print(f"\nLooking for {desc} ({width}x{height}x{bitplanes})...")
        print(f"  Expected size: {total_size} bytes")
        
        found_for_config = 0
        
        for offset in scan_offsets:
            if offset + total_size > len(data):
                continue
            
            # Quick check: does this look like graphics?
            chunk = data[offset:offset + total_size]
            zero_count = chunk.count(0)
            ff_count = chunk.count(0xff)
            
            # Graphics typically have moderate variance
            if zero_count > total_size * 0.95 or ff_count > total_size * 0.95:
                continue
            
            # Try to extract
            try:
                img = try_extract_image(data, width, height, bitplanes, offset)
                if img:
                    # Save image
                    filename = f"gfx_{offset:06x}_{width}x{height}x{bitplanes}.png"
                    img.save(output_dir / filename)
                    found_for_config += 1
                    found_count += 1
                    
                    if found_for_config <= 3:  # Only print first few
                        print(f"    ✓ Found @ 0x{offset:06x} -> {filename}")
            except Exception as e:
                pass
        
        if found_for_config > 3:
            print(f"    ... and {found_for_config - 3} more")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print(f"Extracted {found_count} potential graphics")
    print(f"Output: {output_dir}/")
    
    return found_count

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: extract_graphics.py <adf_file> [output_dir]")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    adf_file = Path(sys.argv[1])
    output_dir = Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else Path('extracted_gfx')
    
    scan_for_graphics(adf_file, output_dir)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

hunkstalker-kult-atari-st-pc-port-docs-c.text:
# Core importado y delta del port

El core C vive en `lib/kult-core/`, importado del repositorio
[kult-atari-st-c](https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c) mediante
`git subtree`.

- Última importación: commit `94c0be1` del repo C (T-022; `load_resource_list_c`).
- Importación inicial: commit `beebb52` (subtree con `--squash`).
- El build del port usa `lib/kult-core/src` y `lib/kult-core/include`.
- Las herramientas y tests del core viven también en el subtree.
- No se compilan `lib/kult-core/docs`, `test` ni `tools` salvo que se invoquen
  explícitamente.

## Delta local del port

Estos ficheros del core llevan cambios propios del port:

- `lib/kult-core/src/commands.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/dispatch.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/handlers.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/input.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/loop.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/mode.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/text.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/video.c`
- `lib/kult-core/include/kult_port.h`

Los cambios son:

1. Instrumentación de diagnóstico (`kult_diag_*`/`kult_text_ev`): llamadas
   acotadas en el core; la implementación vive en `platform/diag.c` y en
   el diferencial son no-op. Ver `DIAGNOSTICO.md`.
2. Espera del sample 0x1f al final de la puerta (`mode.c`), específica del
   timing del port.
3. Hooks/declaraciones no-op para que el core siga compilando sin el port.

## Actualizar desde el repo C

```sh
git subtree pull \
  --prefix=lib/kult-core \
  https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c.git main \
  --squash
```

Si el pull toca alguno de los ficheros del delta, hay que resolver el conflicto
manteniendo la instrumentación y el shim del port. No se debe borrar el delta
sin revisar antes el comportamiento del port.

## Regenerar

```sh
make addrs
make mapa
make regscan
```

`make addrs` y `make mapa` escriben en `lib/kult-core/include` y
`lib/kult-core/docs/mapa`.

# CMake del ejecutable del port (M7/T-070, macOS T-136). El core no se toca:
# este build enlaza lib/kult-core/src (juego) + boot/ + platform/ + app/, con
# `platform/include` el primero para sombrear os.h/hw.h/psg.h/sched.h con la HAL
# de PC. El Makefile sigue siendo el build del core y del diferencial (`make test`).
#
#   Linux:  cmake -S . -B build-linux -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ...
#   Windows (cross MinGW): ver cmake/mingw-w64.cmake y docs/BUILD.md.
#   macOS Universal 2: ver docs/BUILD.md y tools/build_macos.sh.
#
# Targets: `kult` (headless) y `kult-sdl` (ventana/audio SDL3). En Windows,
# `kult-sdl` sale como kult.exe y el headless como kult-headless.exe. En macOS,
# `kult-sdl` produce Kult.app.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET)
  set(CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET "11.0" CACHE STRING "Minimum macOS version")
endif()
project(kult VERSION 1.2.1 LANGUAGES C)

# Ruta a la SDL3 compartida que se empaqueta en Linux/macOS (se puede pasar con
# -DKULT_SDL3_LIB=...). En Windows se usa third_party/SDL3-.../SDL3.dll.
set(KULT_SDL3_LIB "" CACHE FILEPATH "SDL3 shared library to bundle on Linux/macOS")

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING "Build type" FORCE)
endif()

# ---- fuentes (espejo de PORT_SRC del Makefile) ------------------------------
file(GLOB KULT_CORE_SRC     CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/src/*.c)
file(GLOB KULT_BOOT_SRC     CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/boot/*.c)
file(GLOB KULT_PLATFORM_SRC CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/*.c)
# La entrada/salida SDL (ventana/audio) sólo va al target `kult-sdl`; la copia
# de traza T-073c no se compila en el build estándar. Con KULT_DIAG_TRACE=ON
# se sustituye lib/kult-core/src/dispatch.c por platform/dispatch_trace.c: escribe Y/V de
# todo el guion (sin depender de F12) para diagnosticar una run completa.
option(KULT_DIAG_TRACE "Usar dispatch_trace.c (traza Y/V completa)" OFF)
list(REMOVE_ITEM KULT_PLATFORM_SRC
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/video_sdl.c
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/audio_sdl.c
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/mac_dialog.c
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/dispatch_trace.c)
if(KULT_DIAG_TRACE)
  list(REMOVE_ITEM KULT_CORE_SRC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/src/dispatch.c)
  list(APPEND KULT_PLATFORM_SRC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/dispatch_trace.c)
endif()

# T-073b: solo el core se instrumenta para cobrar el coste medido por función.
# El diferencial (make test) no usa este CMake y sigue sin instrumentar.
set_source_files_properties(${KULT_CORE_SRC}
  PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-finstrument-functions")
# El cursor software del core se conserva, pero se renombra para que el port
# pueda envolverlo y componer una copia de presentación/captura.
set_source_files_properties(
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/src/cursor.c
  PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "cursor_draw=kult_core_cursor_draw;cursor_restore=kult_core_cursor_restore")

add_library(kultport STATIC ${KULT_CORE_SRC} ${KULT_BOOT_SRC} ${KULT_PLATFORM_SRC})
# `platform/include` PRIMERO: sombrea os.h/hw.h/psg.h/sched.h del kit.
target_include_directories(kultport PUBLIC
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/include
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/boot
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/include
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/tools/recreate_kit/include)
target_compile_options(kultport PRIVATE -O2 -Wall -Wextra)
target_compile_definitions(kultport PUBLIC KULT_VERSION="${PROJECT_VERSION}")
if(WIN32)
  # platform/log.c usa GetConsoleWindow/MessageBoxA (diagnóstico visible).
  target_link_libraries(kultport PUBLIC user32)
endif()

# ---- ejecutables ------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(kult app/main.c)
target_link_libraries(kult PRIVATE kultport)

add_executable(kult-sdl app/main.c platform/video_sdl.c platform/audio_sdl.c)
target_compile_definitions(kult-sdl PRIVATE HAVE_SDL3)
target_include_directories(kult-sdl PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets)
if(APPLE)
  target_sources(kult-sdl PRIVATE platform/mac_dialog.c)
endif()

# SDL3: primero el paquete de CMake; si no está (Linux mínimo), pkg-config.
find_package(SDL3 CONFIG QUIET)
if(SDL3_FOUND)
  target_link_libraries(kult-sdl PRIVATE kultport SDL3::SDL3)
else()
  find_package(PkgConfig REQUIRED)
  pkg_check_modules(SDL3 REQUIRED IMPORTED_TARGET sdl3)
  target_link_libraries(kult-sdl PRIVATE kultport PkgConfig::SDL3)
endif()

# ---- icono de la app (recurso del .exe en Windows) --------------------------
if(WIN32)
  set(KULT_ICON_RC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/kult_icon.rc)
  set(CMAKE_RC_FLAGS "${CMAKE_RC_FLAGS} -I\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets\"")
  # windres referencia el .ico por ruta; sin esto, regenerarlo no recompila el
  # recurso y el .exe se queda con el icono anterior.
  set_property(SOURCE ${KULT_ICON_RC} PROPERTY OBJECT_DEPENDS
               ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/kult_icon.ico)
  target_sources(kult-sdl PRIVATE ${KULT_ICON_RC})
  set_target_properties(kult-sdl PROPERTIES WIN32_EXECUTABLE TRUE OUTPUT_NAME kult)
  set_target_properties(kult PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME kult-headless)
endif()

# ---- empaquetado de release -------------------------------------------------
# El paquete NO lleva assets del juego: el usuario aporta sus STX en data/.
# kult-headless sigue siendo un target de desarrollo, pero no se empaqueta.
if(APPLE)
  set_target_properties(kult-sdl PROPERTIES
    OUTPUT_NAME "Kult"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE TRUE
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_INFO_PLIST "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/macos/Info.plist.in"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_BUNDLE_NAME "Kult"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_GUI_IDENTIFIER "com.hunkstalker.kult"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_ICON_FILE "kult.icns"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_BUNDLE_VERSION "${PROJECT_VERSION}"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_SHORT_VERSION_STRING "${PROJECT_VERSION}"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_COPYRIGHT "MIT"
    INSTALL_RPATH "@executable_path/../Frameworks")
  if(KULT_SDL3_LIB)
    set(KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB "${KULT_SDL3_LIB}")
  else()
    find_library(KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB NAMES SDL3 libSDL3.0.dylib)
  endif()
  if(NOT KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB OR NOT EXISTS "${KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB}")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "macOS: define -DKULT_SDL3_LIB=<ruta a libSDL3.0.dylib>")
  endif()
  get_filename_component(KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_REAL "${KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB}" REALPATH)
endif()

if(APPLE)
  install(TARGETS kult-sdl BUNDLE DESTINATION .)
else()
  install(TARGETS kult-sdl RUNTIME DESTINATION .)
endif()
install(FILES
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/Kult Settings.txt"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/Kult Settings.png"
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/LICENSE
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
  DESTINATION .)
if(NOT APPLE)
  install(FILES ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/language.data DESTINATION data)

install(DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/LICENSES DESTINATION .)

      ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/third_party/SDL3-3.4.10-win32-x64/SDL3.dll)
  if(EXISTS ${KULT_SDL3_DLL})
    install(FILES ${KULT_SDL3_DLL} DESTINATION .)
  else()
    message(WARNING "falta ${KULT_SDL3_DLL}: el paquete no incluirá SDL3.dll")
  endif()

  install(DIRECTORY DESTINATION saves)

if(APPLE)

          DESTINATION "Kult.app/Contents/Frameworks" RENAME "libSDL3.0.dylib")
  install(FILES ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/language.data

"""Extracts all assets from the Manic Miner CPC disk image into ManicMiner/Assets."""
import os, json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
from gameimg import pristine_full
from render import HW, pix
from PIL import Image

OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'ManicMiner', 'Assets')
ROM = '/usr/share/caprice32/rom/cpc464.rom'   # firmware font (not on the disk)
m = pristine_full()
w16 = lambda a: m[a] | m[a + 1] << 8

def pens(h): return [h[4], h[3], h[2], h[1]]  # pen0..pen3 from header bytes 16..19 -> see below

def level(i):

meowmuhmuhcow-schicksalsklinge-bauen-bau.text:
# BLADEM.EXE selbst bauen

Dieser Ordner baut aus dem rekonstruierten Quelltext die Spiel-EXE der *Schicksalsklinge* (DSA 1, Attic 1992) und
vergleicht sie Byte für Byte mit dem Original. Am Ende steht im Fenster:

> **BYTEGLEICH mit dem Original**

## Einmal vorbereiten

| Schritt | Was |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Python für Windows** installieren: [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/), beim Installieren **„Add python.exe to PATH“** ankreuzen |
| 2 | Borland C++ 3.1 nach `Compiler\` (BIN, INCLUDE, LIB) und `SCHICKM.EXE` aus der GOG-Installation nach `Original\`, siehe `START_HIER.md` |

DOSBox ist schon da, nämlich das aus der GOG-Schicksalsklinge (`Realms of Arkania\DOSBOX\DOSBox.exe`).

**Ohne Installation:** das „Windows embeddable package (64-bit)“ von python.org nach `Bauen\python\` entpacken, sodass
`Bauen\python\python.exe` existiert. BAUEN.bat nimmt es dann von selbst.

## Bauen

Doppelklick auf **`BAUEN.bat`**. Dauer etwa eine halbe bis zwei Minuten, vier Schritte `[1/4] … [4/4]`.

| Ergebnis | Wo |
|---|---|
| gebaute EXE | `Build\BLADEM.EXE` (dazu `BLADEM.MAP`) |
| Protokoll | `Build\bau.log` |
| Arbeitsordner (wird bei jedem Bau geleert) | `%TEMP%\schicksalsklinge_bau` |

## Fix-Fassungen (Fehlerbehebungen)

`BAUEN.bat wichtig` bzw. `BAUEN.bat alles` baut nach dem normalen Bau zusätzlich eine EXE mit eingeschalteten
Fehlerbehebungen (Schalter `FIX_nnnn` in `Quelle\s_fix.h`, Liste mit Gründen in `FIXES.md`). Dauer etwa so lang wie
ein zweiter Bau. **Alle Behebungen sind im Spiel ungetestet – Tester willkommen.**

| Aufruf | Ergebnis | Inhalt |
|---|---|---|
| `BAUEN.bat wichtig` | `Build\BLADEM_FIX_WICHTIG.EXE` | Behebungen der Kategorien *kritisch* und *mittel* (`FIX_BUGS=1`) |
| `BAUEN.bat alles` | `Build\BLADEM_FIX_ALLES.EXE` | zusätzlich alle *egal*-Fehler (`FIX_BUGS=2`) |

Gestartet werden sie mit `BLADEM_FIX_WICHTIG_STARTEN.bat` bzw. `BLADEM_FIX_ALLES_STARTEN.bat` im Projektordner
(neben `BLADEM_STARTEN.bat`). Die Startdateien kopieren die Fix-EXE als `BLADEM.EXE` nach `Build\Fix_Wichtig` bzw.
`Build\Fix_Alles` (DOS kennt nur 8.3-Namen) und legen Spielstände in eigene Ordner
`Build\Testspielstaende_Fix_Wichtig` bzw. `Build\Testspielstaende_Fix_Alles`.

Der normale Bau läuft im Fix-Modus immer mit: er muss weiterhin **BYTEGLEICH** melden und ist die Vergleichsfassung.
Der Fix-Bau übersetzt alle Module mit `-DFIX_BUGS=1` bzw. `=2`, füllt geänderte residente Module auf ihre
Originallänge auf (`Werkzeuge\segpad.py`; wird eines länger, bricht der Bau ab), linkt und prüft mit
`Werkzeuge\fixcheck.py`: residente Segmente an gleicher Stelle, Datensegment Byte für Byte unverändert, alle
Overlay-Einsprünge zeigen auf dieselben Funktionen. Die Spielstände bleiben mit dem Original austauschbar (keine
Behebung ändert Strukturen oder das Spielstandformat).

Weitere Optionen: `BAUEN.bat alles --exploits-lassen` (Fehler, die dem Spieler nützen, bleiben drin, `FIX_EXPLOITS=0`),
`BAUEN.bat alles --fixflags "-DFIX_0222=0"` (einzelne Schalter übersteuern). Die EXE heißt dann trotzdem
`BLADEM_FIX_ALLES.EXE`.

## Was der Bau macht

| Schritt | Was passiert |
|---|---|
| 1 | Compiler und `Quelle\` in den Arbeitsordner kopieren, `TURBOC.CFG` auf `C:\BC` setzen, `DATUM.COM` anlegen (Datum 12.01.1994, steht in der EXE) |
| 2 | alle Module in der Reihenfolge von `Quelle\build.bat` übersetzen: 106 × BCC 3.1 (`-mlarge -O- -c -1 -Y/-Yo`), 5 × TASM 3.1 – immer im selben Durchgang und in derselben Reihenfolge (BCC liest in seltenen Fällen nicht vorbelegten Speicher, siehe `Analyse\LEITFADEN_C.md`) |
| 3 | in der Entwicklungsumgebung linken wie Attic: `BC.EXE /b BLADEM.PRJ` |
| 4 | Vergleich mit `Original\SCHICKM.EXE` (MD5 `4ce035f95ead01a8b2553b4487544e5d`) |

Wer eine Datei in `Quelle\` ändert, baut mit seiner Änderung. Die EXE ist dann natürlich nicht mehr bytegleich.

## Meldungen

| Meldung | Bedeutung |
|---|---|
| `BYTEGLEICH mit dem Original` | alles richtig |
| `ABWEICHUNG vom Original: erste Differenz bei Byte …` | gebaut, aber nicht gleich (Quelle geändert?) |
| `Uebersetzungsfehler` | ein Modul übersetzt nicht, die Zeilen stehen im Protokoll |
| `Fix-Modus: ... passt nicht in sein residentes Segment` | eine Behebung macht ein residentes Modul länger – so nicht baubar |
| `Fix-Modus: fixcheck meldet Fehler` | die Fix-EXE wäre mit dem Original nicht verträglich, sie wird nicht ausgegeben |
| `Borland C++ 3.1 nicht gefunden` | `Compiler\BIN\BCC.EXE` fehlt |
| `DOSBox nicht gefunden` | GOG-Pfad anders: DOSBox-Ordner nach `Bauen\DOSBox\` kopieren oder `--dosbox PFAD` |
| `Python 3 wurde nicht gefunden` | Schritt 1 oben fehlt |

## Optionen

`BAUEN.bat` reicht Optionen an `bauen.py` weiter, z. B. `BAUEN.bat --sichtbar`.

| Option | Wirkung |
|---|---|
| `wichtig` / `alles` | zusätzlich die Fix-EXE bauen (siehe oben) |
| `--exploits-lassen`, `--fixflags "..."` | nur mit `wichtig`/`alles`, siehe oben |
| `--sichtbar` | DOSBox-Fenster zeigen |
| `--dosbox PFAD` | andere DOSBox |
| `--compiler ORDNER` | Compiler woanders |
| `--baudir ORDNER` | anderer Arbeitsordner |
| `--projekt ORDNER` | Projektordner, falls `Bauen\` woanders liegt |

`Build\Fix_Alles` (DOS kennt nur 8.3-Namen) und legen Spielstände in eigene Ordner
`Build\Testspielstaende_Fix_Wichtig` bzw. `Build\Testspielstaende_Fix_Alles`.

Der normale Bau läuft im Fix-Modus immer mit: er muss weiterhin **BYTEGLEICH** melden und liefert die
Vergleichsfassung, über die der Fix-Bau die Linknamen zuordnet. Die Fix-EXE kann nicht bytegleich sein; geprüft wird
stattdessen (`fixcheck`): residente Segmente an gleicher Stelle, Datensegment unverändert, alle Overlay-Einsprünge
vorhanden. Die Spielstände bleiben mit dem Original austauschbar (keine Behebung ändert Strukturen oder das

## Was der Bau benutzt

| Option | Wirkung |

jamescarruthers-cyclone-re-readme-md.text:
# Cyclone (Vortex Software, 1985) — reverse engineering

Complete reverse engineering of the ZX Spectrum 48K game *Cyclone* (Costa Panayi / Vortex), from the
TAP image in `../original/`. All 4,300 executed instructions and every data region in $5B00–$FFFF are
identified and annotated.

The 3D remake built from this work is in [`../remake`](../remake/README.md).

## Contents

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `ctl/cyclone.ctl` | Master SkoolKit control file (merged from `frontend`, `core1`, `core2`, `core3`, `data`) |
| `build/cyclone.skool`, `build/cyclone.asm` | Annotated disassembly (skool + assembler listing) |
| `build/html/cyclone/index.html` | Browsable HTML disassembly with cross-references |
| `notes/frontend.md` | Boot, loader, menu, controls, main loop, game flow, crates/survivors/winch |
| `notes/core1.md` | Variable glossary ($7500–$7563), view-window builder, terrain projection, shadow |
| `notes/core2.md` | Input, flight model, fuel/time/altimeter bars, HUD, aircraft, interrupt sound |
| `notes/core3.md` | Collision/landing, RNG, sea waves, helicopter sprite, map screen, cyclone, death |
| `notes/data.md` | World/island data format, tile column tables, charset, sprites, fonts, asset files |
| `assets/` | Extracted graphics, world grid (768×768), fonts, HUD, verification renders |
| `snapshots/` | `cyclone.tap`, `init.z80` (canonical post-init image), plus menu/info/in-game states |
| `tools/` | Emulation driver (scripted keys), disassembly helpers, asset extractors, render verifier, `reftrace.py` (original-vs-remake state comparison and autopilot), `export_remake_data.py` |

Rebuild: `sna2skool.py -H -c ctl/cyclone.ctl snapshots/init.z80 > build/cyclone.skool`, then
`skool2html.py -H -d build/html build/cyclone.skool` / `skool2asm.py -H build/cyclone.skool`.

Evidence tags used in the notes: **CODE** (read from disassembly), **OBSERVED** (seen in emulation under
SkoolKit's simulator with scripted input and breakpoints), **INFERRED** (interpretation).

## Summary of the machine

* **Loading**: BASIC → SCREEN$ → 512-byte loader at $FE00 → 40,630-byte block at $5FDC. `USR 65176` →
  $FE98 → init $F74E: relocates the main loop to $5B00 (printer buffer) and the crate shuffler to $5EEC,
  fills an IM2 table at $FF00 with $F3 (vector $F3F3 = `JP $83C2`, hidden inside the winch routine),
  `IM 2`, menu at $E280. The 16 Z80 snapshot variants are the same program in different saved states.
* **Timing**: no HALT; the main loop free-runs at ~4–5.6 TV frames per iteration (≈ 9–11 Hz). Every game
  timer counts *iterations*. The 50 Hz interrupt only makes sound (rotor chop, winch click, crash noise).
* **RNG** ($8B74): `seed' = (254·(seed+1) mod 65537) − 1`, seed in ROM SYSVAR SEED $5C76.

## Game rules (reconciled across all notes)

* **World**: 768×768 tile cells (3×3 sectors of 256), 14 islands stored as rectangular blocks in
  $9300–$DDFF (128-byte rows), placed by the 20-byte records at $F230. Everything else is sea. The view
  is a 23×22 window of the 23×29 buffer whose origin is (X,Y) = ($7500,$7502); the helicopter's ground
  cell is (X+11, Y+14). The map grid used by the cyclone/map screen is 23×22 cells of 32×32 tiles.
* **Projection**: each tile code expands into a *column* of 8×8 chars (pages $63+k north, $6C+k
  south; $FE skip, $FF end). Level k is drawn k rows above the tile; nearer rows overwrite. This is
  exactly an orthographic view at 45° from the south: level-k chars are south-facing cube faces, the
  last char is the top face. The south view is the window rotated 180° using the second page set
  (north faces). Only two views exist (N key toggles).
* **Helicopter**: 8 headings (45° steps; a turn takes 4 iterations and shows an odd in-between frame);
  while speed ($7527, 0–7) > 0 it moves exactly 1 tile per iteration per axis (diagonals √2 faster).
  Speed is only momentum: 6 iterations of coasting after releasing thrust. Climb/descent ramps
  1→2→3 px per iteration; altitude 0–60 px (8 px = one level). Landed state snaps altitude to ×8.
* **Collision/landing** ($8A7A): footprint = 3×3 cells; terrain class = number of thresholds
  `0F 10 2E 30 56 58 89 8C A5 B2 C2 D0 D9 E4 EC F0 F6 FF` ≤ tile (2 classes per level, odd = object on
  top). `alt>>2 ≥ class` clears a cell. Partial clearance = crash; touching at descent rate 3 = crash;
  touchdown requires every top char to be landable; all 9 helipad chars ($83/$89) = on pad.
* **Fuel**: 40 bar lines, −1 per 49 iterations whenever not on the base pad; +1 per iteration on the
  pad. Empty: forced descent, no thrust/climb; landing empty away from the pad = "NO FUEL" (lose a life).
  Each life starts on the pad with an empty tank.
* **Time**: 40 lines (+1 tick), one per 255 iterations in round 1, 15 fewer per later round. Running out
  = "NO TIME" = game over. Time bonus at round start: 40 points per remaining line.
* **Crates/survivors**: 5 crates on random sites of 38 (shuffled continuously while the menu waits);
  survivors on all 45 survivor sites each round. Hover low over one: the rope drops, the object is
  hooked (map tile replaced) and reeled in; +250 per crate, +50 per survivor on arrival. Five crates and
  landing on the Base island pad completes the round: bonus 2-step add = 352/288/224 for 0/1/2 lives
  lost (an original bug passes 102 to the second add instead of 250−64n).
* **Lives**: 3 per round (restored every round). Death: 24-iteration explosion, icon turns red, respawn
  on base pad; 3 lost = straight back to the menu. A+G abandons.
* **Cyclone**: invisible except through effects. Map-grid position (1..21, 1..20), starts in a random
  corner; one grid step every 25 iterations using 16 equiprobable direction regimes (re-picked every 9
  steps or at edges). Chebyshev distance d (≤15) sets WIND FORCE = 16−d, DANGER flashes at d<6, and at
  d<5 (round 1; d<6 later) the controls get random bits ORed in (`RND & $1A` at d≥4, `& $1B` at 2–3,
  forced down+left at d<2).
* **Aircraft**: 19 planes, 2 tiles per iteration in 16 directions, steered by a 15-step script (one
  step per 28 iterations, some steps respawn a plane at its entry point). Only the first plane within
  ±12/±15 tiles is drawn; its height level ($87EF) creeps one level per iteration towards the
  helicopter's level, and touching it at the same level is a crash. BEWARE AIRCRAFT flashes within
  ±22/±25.

## Reconciliation notes
* $87EF is the **aircraft's** height level (core2, verified by an emulated collision through the
  $8B36 "very tall" branch); core3's notes call it the helicopter's level — that is superseded.
* Cyclone "cells" (core3) are map-grid cells of 32×32 tiles; the world itself is 768×768 tiles (data).
* There is no cyclone sprite anywhere: traced reads during flight, map and crash never touch one.

jamescarruthers-cyclone-remake-readme-md.text:
# Cyclone 3D — a Rust + wgpu remake of Cyclone (Vortex Software, 1985)

A recreation of the ZX Spectrum game *Cyclone* (Costa Panayi) in true 3D. It keeps the original's
look, rules and timing. The reverse engineering it is built on is in [`../re`](../re/README.md).

## Build and run

```sh
cargo run --release
```

Requires a Rust toolchain (tested with 1.98) and a GPU supported by wgpu (Metal, Vulkan or DX12).

### Browser version

```sh
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.129   # must match wasm-bindgen in Cargo.lock
web/build.sh                                       # builds web/dist
python3 -m http.server -d web/dist 8080            # then open http://localhost:8080
```

`web/dist` is a static site (`index.html`, `cyclone.js`, `cyclone_bg.wasm`: 4.3 MB, 1.2 MB
gzipped) that any web server can host. It uses WebGPU where the browser has it and falls back
to WebGL 2. Click the game (or press a key) to give it the keyboard; sound starts with the first
key press, as browsers require. The Wireframe button does the same as F2; the Fullscreen button
replaces F11.

## Controls

The game reads the keyboard exactly as the original did.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `1`–`5` | up (climb; first press takes off) |
| `Q`–`T` | down |
| `O` / `P` | turn left / right (45° steps) |
| `Shift`, `Z`, `X`, `C`, `V` | forward (thrust) |
| `N` | view north ↔ south (the camera swings round) |
| `[` / `]` | rotate the view 45° anticlockwise / clockwise (the camera swings round, as for `N`) |
| `M` | map ↔ main screen |
| `A` + `G` | abandon the game |
| Menu `1`–`6` | information, keyboard, Interface 2, Kempston, Protek/AGF, start |
| Arrows + right Ctrl | Kempston joystick (choose option 4) |
| `F1` | orthographic "classic" camera ↔ perspective |
| `F2` | textured ↔ wireframe 3D view (a diagonal wipe moves between them) |
| `F11` | fullscreen |

Objective (from the original information screen): collect five crates, then return to base and land
on the helipad. Rescue survivors for extra points. Watch the fuel (F) and time (T) bars, avoid the
aircraft, and stay away from the cyclone: you can't see it, but the WIND FORCE bar and DANGER warning
show how close it is.

## How it works

* **Game logic: a port of the original code** (`src/game.rs`). Each routine of the Z80 program is
  translated one to one, and its doc comment gives the original address. The port keeps the
  original 64 KB memory layout: variables at `$7500`, the self-modified operands, the tile store,
  the view buffer and the screen all live at their original addresses, in an image of the game
  after loading (`data/mem.bin`). Quirks are kept, for example the round-bonus bug, the altimeter's
  `$4F` comparison and the aircraft-collision comparison.
* **Timing**: the original main loop free-runs at about 9–10 iterations per second, and every game
  timer counts iterations. The port is straight-line code: beeps block, the same as ROM BEEPER, and
  a virtual clock drives the 50 Hz interrupt (rotor chop, winch click and crash noise) and paces
  the game against the wall clock (`src/sys.rs`). The routines that pass time are `async`. On the
  desktop the game runs on its own thread and the pacing point sleeps. In the browser the game
  is a future polled once per animation frame, and the pacing point waits until the clock catches
  up.
* **Sound**: 1-bit beeper tones rendered through cpal (`src/audio.rs`).
* **3D world** (`src/world.rs`, `src/render.rs`, `src/shader.wgsl`). The original draws each map
  tile as a column of 8×8 characters (pages `$63+k` for the north view, `$6C+k` for the south view).
  Geometrically that is an oblique view of a stack of cubes, so each column becomes real cubes:
  * the char at level k textures that cube's south face, the south-view char its north face, and the
    last char the top face;
  * trees, crates and survivors are upright cards that turn to face the camera;
  * all textures are the original glyphs in their attribute colours, and cyan "sky" pixels are cut
    out. So is the paper of the object cards: it is the background the original drew behind the
    object, which the 3D view now shows for real (so shadows pass behind trees). Back faces are
    culled, so you see the sea through a cut-out pixel, not the inside of the cube;
  * the red-roofed houses (two tiles deep: striped roof char on the front row, checked on the
    back) get gable roofs, with the ridge between the rows; the original draws the roof flat.
    Their end walls always show windows (the original swaps window and plain chars between the
    north and south views);
  * a terrace's corner on the coast, which the original rounds off with a diagonally cut top
    char, is cut through its whole height: a triangular prism with a diagonal cliff wall, so no
    square wall sticks up past the cut when the camera turns;
  * shadows are cut along the tile edges, so each piece lies on its own tile's surface (and on
    the slope of a roof, and along a cut corner's diagonal).

  With the orthographic camera (F1) the 45° view reproduces the original screen almost pixel for
  pixel. The perspective camera is the default.
* **Sprites** (`src/scene.rs`): the helicopter, aircraft, shadows, rope and crash debris use the
  original frames. The frame is picked from the heading relative to the camera, so the helicopter
  and aircraft turn properly as the camera swings round. Positions are interpolated between game
  iterations.
* **HUD, menus and map** are drawn by the ported routines into the emulated Spectrum screen memory,
  then shown on top of the 3D view (`src/zx.rs`).

## Verification against the original

`../re/tools/reftrace.py` runs the original program under SkoolKit's Z80 simulator. It feeds the
same per-iteration keyboard input to the original and to the port (`cyclone --trace`) and compares
the full game state at every main-loop iteration: all variables, score, aircraft table, the tile
store, the HUD screen memory and the footprint under the helicopter.

```sh
python -I ../re/tools/reftrace.py gen 1 3000 s.txt                     # random flight
python -I ../re/tools/reftrace.py run ../re/snapshots/info.z80 s.txt start.bin rs.txt > ref.trace
python -I ../re/tools/reftrace.py auto ../re/snapshots/info.z80 6000 a.txt start.bin rs.txt > ref.trace   # autopilot
cargo run --release -- --trace start.bin rs.txt > rust.trace
python -I ../re/tools/reftrace.py diff ref.trace rust.trace
```

Results:

* Three random flights: identical.
* An autopilot run of 4,845 iterations: identical. It collects crates with the winch, completes a
  round with its bonus, plays the next round and ends in game over.

The only difference is the RNG seed at the start of a new life. The original's crash noise calls the
RNG from the interrupt handler a timing-dependent number of times, so the harness re-syncs the seed
there.

## Other modes

* `cyclone --video START.bin SCRIPT OUT.mp4 [ITERATIONS] [N-presses] [W-toggles]`: renders a
  gameplay MP4 with sound (needs ffmpeg; set `CYCLONE_FFMPEG` to point at the binary).
  `N-presses` and `W-toggles` are comma-separated iterations: at each N press the camera swings
  round, and at each W toggle the 3D view wipes between textured and wireframe. The showcase is
  the autopilot run (`reftrace.py auto`, see above) with
  `1700 260,340 515,690,1520,1620`.
* `cyclone --orbit ISLAND DIR [FRAMES] [PITCH] [STRETCH]`: orbit renders of an island (0–13).
* `cyclone --wipe ISLAND OUT.mp4 [SECONDS]`: an orbit of an island that starts textured, then
  wipes to the wireframe view (needs ffmpeg, as `--video`).
* `cyclone --shot X Y SOUTH ORTHO OUT.ppm`: the in-game camera at a given window origin.
* `cyclone --demo SCRIPT DIR [EVERY]`: composed screenshots from a scripted game.
* `CYCLONE_SNAPSHOT=SECONDS:FILE.ppm cyclone`: save one frame from the live window, then quit.

## Data

`data/` holds the original game's memory after loading (with the 256 ROM bytes the sea-wave code
reads as random data) and screens captured from the original: menu, information, map and the
loading screen. They are regenerated by `../re/tools/export_remake_data.py`. These are the
original copyrighted assets, for personal and preservation use.

jamescarruthers-cyclone-re-tools-reftrac.text:
"""Reference trace of the ORIGINAL game for verifying the Rust port.

Runs the original code under SkoolKit's C simulator from $5B00 (game start) with a scripted
keyboard, and prints the game state at every main-loop iteration ($5B3C) in exactly the format
of `cyclone --trace` (remake/src/trace.rs).

  python -I reftrace.py gen SEED N SCRIPT.txt          # make a random flight script
  python -I reftrace.py run SNAPSHOT SCRIPT.txt START.bin RUST_SCRIPT.txt > ref.trace
  python -I reftrace.py diff ref.trace rust.trace

`run` writes START.bin (memory at $5B00) for the Rust side and RUST_SCRIPT.txt (the script
plus the original's RNG seed at each iteration, because the original's crash noise calls the
RNG from the interrupt handler, which depends on exact interrupt timing).
"""
import random
import sys

from skoolkit.simutils import from_snapshot, PC, SP
from skoolkit.snapshot import Snapshot
from skoolkit import CSimulator
from skoolkit.simulator import Simulator
from skoolkit.trace import Tracer

ROWS = ["SHIFT Z X C V", "A S D F G", "Q W E R T", "1 2 3 4 5", "0 9 8 7 6",
        "P O I U Y", "ENTER L K J H", "SPACE SYM M N B"]
KEYMAP = {k: (r, b) for r, row in enumerate(ROWS) for b, k in enumerate(row.split())}


def keys_line(keys):
    rows = [0] * 8
    for k in keys.split():
        r, b = KEYMAP[k]
        rows[r] |= 1 << b
    return ' '.join(f'{v:02X}' for v in rows)


def gen(seed, n, out):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    lines = [''] * 45 + ['1'] * 12           # refuel on the pad, then climb
    acts = ['X', 'X O', 'X P', 'X 1', 'X Q', '', 'O', 'P', '1', 'Q', 'X', 'X', 'X 1', 'X O 1']
    while len(lines) < n:
        r = rnd.random()
        if r < 0.04:
            lines += ['M'] + [''] * rnd.randint(4, 30) + ['M']
        elif r < 0.08:
            lines += ['N']
        else:
            a = rnd.choice(acts)
            lines += [a] * rnd.randint(2, 40)
    with open(out, 'w') as f:
        for l in lines[:n]:
            f.write(keys_line(l) + '\n')


def fnv(bs):
    h = 0x811C9DC5
    for b in bs:
        h ^= b
        h = (h * 0x01000193) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return h


def pixel_addr(line, col):
    return 0x4000 | ((line & 0xC0) << 5) | ((line & 7) << 8) | ((line & 0x38) << 2) | col


# render-only scratch pointers (762C/7BB8/86AF/8D5D are replaced by the 3D renderer) and the
# interrupt's rotor sound phase
SCRATCH = [0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0E, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B, 0x2C,
           0x3C, 0x3D, 0x3E, 0x3F, 0x5D]

HUD_ADDRS = []
for row in range(24):
    for col in (range(32) if row >= 22 else range(24, 32)):
        HUD_ADDRS += [pixel_addr(row * 8 + line, col) for line in range(8)] + [0x5800 + row * 32 + col]


def state_line(i, m):
    hx = lambda a, n: ''.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in m[a:a + n])
    v = list(m[0x7500:0x7564])
    for o in SCRATCH:
        v[o] = 0
    return (f"{i} seed={hx(0x5C76, 2)} v={''.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in v)} score={hx(0x661E, 7)} "
            f"misc={hx(0x87EF, 1)}{hx(0x8A69, 3)}{hx(0x5B93, 1)}{hx(0x828C, 1)}{hx(0x9245, 1)}{hx(0x7A81, 9)} "
            f"air={hx(0xE86C, 95)} store={fnv(m[0x9300:0xDE00]):08X} hud={fnv(m[a] for a in HUD_ADDRS):08X}")


def run(snapshot, script, start_bin, rust_script):
    snap = Snapshot.get(snapshot)
    sim = from_snapshot(CSimulator or Simulator, snap, {}, {'ay': [None] * 16}, {'fast_djnz': False, 'fast_ldir': False})
    tracer = Tracer(sim, 0, 0, 0, [0] * 16, 0, False)
    sim.set_tracer(tracer)
    m, r = sim.memory, sim.registers
    r[PC] = 0x5B00
    r[SP] = 0xFEFF
    open(start_bin, 'wb').write(bytes(m[:65536]))
    lines = [l.strip() for l in open(script)]
    keyboard = [0] * 8
    tracer.keyboard = keyboard
    out = open(rust_script, 'w')
    pc = 0x5B00
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        t0 = r[25]
        stop, _ = sim.trace(pc, 0x5B3C, 0, t0 + 3500000 * 60, 1, None, None, keyboard, None, None)
        if r[PC] != 0x5B3C:
            print(f'# stopped at {r[PC]:04X} (game over?)', file=sys.stderr)
            break
        print(state_line(i, m))
        sys.stdout.flush()
        rows = [int(x, 16) for x in lines[i].split()]
        for k in range(8):
            keyboard[k] = rows[k]
        out.write(f"{lines[i]} seed={m[0x5C77]:02X}{m[0x5C76]:02X}\n")
        pc = 0x5B3C
        # step one instruction so the next trace call does not stop immediately
        sim.trace(pc, -1, 1, 0, 1, None, None, keyboard, None, None)
        pc = r[PC]
        i += 1
    out.close()


def world_of(m, addr):
    """World cell (x, y) of a tile-store address (via the island records at F230)."""
    a = 0xF230
    while m[a] != 0xFF:
        base = m[a + 10] | m[a + 11] << 8
        w, h = m[a + 3] - m[a + 6] + 1, m[a + 5] - m[a + 8] + 1
        off = addr - base
        if 0 <= off < h * 128 and off % 128 < w:
            return m[a] * 256 + m[a + 6] + off % 128, m[a + 1] * 256 + m[a + 8] + off // 128
        a += 20
    return None


class Autopilot:
    """Flies the original game: refuel, collect every placed crate with the winch, return to
    the base pad and land (completing the round). Decides keys from the game memory."""
    CRATE_TILES = {0x8B: 3, 0x57: 2, 0x2F: 1, 0x0F: 0}

    def __init__(self):
        self.phase = 'refuel'
        self.tap = 0
        self.rounds = 0

    def targets(self, m):
        out = []
        for i in range(38):
            e = 0x5F61 + 3 * i
            if m[e] == 0xFF:
                cell = m[e + 1] | m[e + 2] << 8
                if m[cell] in self.CRATE_TILES:
                    wx, wy = world_of(m, cell)
                    out.append((wx - 11, wy - 14, self.CRATE_TILES[m[cell]]))
        return out

    def keys(self, m):
        w16 = lambda a: m[a] | m[a + 1] << 8
        sx = lambda v: v - 65536 if v >= 32768 else v
        x, y = sx(w16(0x7500)), sx(w16(0x7502))
        alt, heading, speed = m[0x750D], m[0x7506], m[0x7527]
        landed, on_pad, winch = m[0x7515], m[0x752E], m[0x7555]
        k = []
        if landed and self.phase in ('goto', 'descend', 'hold', 'home'):
            self.phase = 'refuel'          # respawned on the pad
        if self.phase == 'refuel':
            if m[0x7518] == 0x1C or not on_pad:
                self.phase = 'goto'
                return '1'                 # take off
            return ''
        if self.phase == 'done':
            return ''
        if self.phase == 'hold':
            if winch == 0 and m[0x7556] == 0:
                self.phase = 'goto'
            return ''
        if self.phase == 'descend':
            if winch:
                self.phase = 'hold'
                return ''
            self.tap ^= 1
            if alt > 8 * self.height + 9 and self.tap:
                return 'Q'
            return ''
        if self.phase == 'land':
            if landed:
                self.phase = 'refuel'
                self.rounds += 1
                return ''
            self.tap ^= 1
            return 'Q' if self.tap else ''
        tg = self.targets(m)
        if self.phase == 'goto':
            if not tg:
                if m[0x7554] == 5:
                    self.phase = 'home'
                else:
                    self.phase = 'done'
                    return ''
        if self.phase == 'home':
            tx, ty, th = 0x139, 0x170, None
        else:
            tx, ty, th = min(tg, key=lambda t: abs(t[0] - x) + abs(t[1] - y))
        if self.phase in ('goto', 'home'):
            if alt < 56:
                k.append('1')
            dx, dy = tx - x, ty - y
            if dx == 0 and dy == 0 and speed == 0:
                self.phase = 'descend' if th is not None else 'land'
                self.height = th
                return ' '.join(k)
            if dx:
                d, r = (4 if dx > 0 else 12), abs(dx)
            else:
                d, r = (8 if dy > 0 else 0), abs(dy)
            if heading != d:
                if speed == 0 and m[0x7521] == 0 and alt >= 40:
                    k.append('P' if (d - heading) % 16 <= 8 else 'O')
            elif alt >= 40:
                if r >= min(speed + 1, 7):
                    k.append('X')
            return ' '.join(k)
        return ''


def auto(snapshot, n, script, start_bin, rust_script):
    """Like `run`, but the keys come from the Autopilot (recorded to SCRIPT)."""
    snap = Snapshot.get(snapshot)
    sim = from_snapshot(CSimulator or Simulator, snap, {}, {'ay': [None] * 16}, {'fast_djnz': False, 'fast_ldir': False})
    tracer = Tracer(sim, 0, 0, 0, [0] * 16, 0, False)
    sim.set_tracer(tracer)
    m, r = sim.memory, sim.registers
    r[PC] = 0x5B00
    r[SP] = 0xFEFF
    open(start_bin, 'wb').write(bytes(m[:65536]))
    keyboard = [0] * 8
    tracer.keyboard = keyboard
    ap = Autopilot()
    out, rec = open(rust_script, 'w'), open(script, 'w')
    pc = 0x5B00
    for i in range(int(n)):
        sim.trace(pc, 0x5B3C, 0, r[25] + 3500000 * 60, 1, None, None, keyboard, None, None)
        if r[PC] != 0x5B3C:
            print(f'# stopped at {r[PC]:04X}', file=sys.stderr)
            break
        print(state_line(i, m))
        line = keys_line(ap.keys(m))
        rows = [int(v, 16) for v in line.split()]
        for j in range(8):
            keyboard[j] = rows[j]
        rec.write(line + '\n')
        out.write(f"{line} seed={m[0x5C77]:02X}{m[0x5C76]:02X}\n")
        sim.trace(0x5B3C, -1, 1, 0, 1, None, None, keyboard, None, None)
        pc = r[PC]
    print(f'# autopilot: phase {ap.phase}, rounds completed {ap.rounds}, score {bytes(m[0x661E:0x6625]).decode()}', file=sys.stderr)


FIELDS = {0x00: 'POS_X', 0x02: 'POS_Y', 0x04: 'VIEW', 0x05: 'CRASHED', 0x06: 'HEADING', 0x07: 'HEADING_DISP',
          0x0D: 'ALT', 0x14: 'TOUCHDOWN', 0x15: 'LANDED', 0x16: 'NO_FUEL', 0x17: 'FUEL_TICK', 0x18: 'FUEL_PTR',
          0x1A: 'CLIMB', 0x1B: 'DESCENT', 0x1C: 'TIME_PTR', 0x1E: 'ALT_PTR', 0x21: 'TURN', 0x22: 'CONTROLS',
          0x26: 'UI', 0x27: 'SPEED', 0x28: 'TIME_TICK', 0x2E: 'ON_PAD', 0x30: 'PLANE_NEAR', 0x33: 'HELI_LEVEL',
          0x3B: 'MOVE_DIR', 0x4B: 'CYC_X', 0x4C: 'CYC_Y', 0x50: 'CYC_DIST', 0x54: 'CRATES', 0x55: 'WINCH'}


def diff(a, b):
    la = [l.split() for l in open(a) if l[0].isdigit()]
    lb = [l.split() for l in open(b) if l[0].isdigit()]
    n = min(len(la), len(lb))
    bad = 0
    resync = 0
    for i in range(n):
        if la[i] != lb[i]:
            fa = dict(x.split('=') for x in la[i][1:])
            fb = dict(x.split('=') for x in lb[i][1:])
            v = bytes.fromhex(fa['v'])
            diffs = [k for k in fa if fa[k] != fb.get(k)]
            # ... and the last crash-sequence frame drew sea waves from that RNG, so the wave
            # codes saved under the helicopter (last 9 bytes of misc) may differ too
            misc_waves_only = fa['misc'][:-18] == fb['misc'][:-18]
            if (set(diffs) <= {'seed', 'misc'} and misc_waves_only and v[0x0D] == 8 and v[0x15] == 1):
                # first iteration of a new life: the original's crash noise called the RNG from
                # the interrupt handler a timing-dependent number of times (resynchronised)
                resync += 1
                continue
            msgs = []
            for k in fa:
                if fa[k] != fb.get(k):
                    if k == 'v':
                        offs = [j for j in range(0, len(fa[k]), 2) if fa[k][j:j + 2] != fb[k][j:j + 2]]
                        msgs.append('v: ' + ', '.join(f"75{o // 2:02X}({FIELDS.get(o // 2, '')}) {fa[k][o:o + 2]}/{fb[k][o:o + 2]}" for o in offs))
                    else:
                        msgs.append(f'{k}: {fa[k]} / {fb.get(k)}')
            print(f'iteration {i}: ' + '; '.join(msgs))
            bad += 1
            if bad >= 8:
                break
    print(f'compared {n} iterations ({len(la)} ref, {len(lb)} rust); '
          f'{"MISMATCH" if bad else "identical"} ({resync} post-crash RNG resyncs)')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    cmd = sys.argv[1]
    if cmd == 'gen':
        gen(int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4])
    elif cmd == 'run':
        run(*sys.argv[2:6])
    elif cmd == 'auto':
        auto(*sys.argv[2:7])
    elif cmd == 'diff':
        diff(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])

kylofon-street-rod-2-sdl3-plan-md.text:
# Street Rod 2 — SDL3 port plan

Same approach as `StreetRod` and the earlier ports: a **faithful C port** here (reverse-engineer →
document → port function by function, original data read at run time), then, once it is
published, a separate **Street Rod 2 Enhanced** repo built on its release. Token efficiency is a first-class
goal: small subtasks, one session each, the cheapest model that can do the job, and the user doing
whatever is cheap for a human and expensive for a model (looking at pictures, playing the game,
driving DOSBox).

**The big lever:** *Street Rod 2: The Next Generation* (1991) is built on the *Street Rod* (1989)
engine, which is already reverse-engineered, specified and ported in `../StreetRod` (faithful,
v0.1.0) and `../StreetRodEnhanced`. So this plan is a **delta port**: match every SR2 function
against SR1 (S1.3), carry names and spec sections over for the identical ones, and spend sessions
only on what changed or is new (AdLib music, `LIB3`, `SR2_*` data, new screens and rules). The
port starts as a copy of `../StreetRod/srport` at its `v0.1.0` tag (S4.1), not from scratch.

## User to-do

What the agents need from you now, most urgent first. Agents add a row when they hand you a task and
remove it when it is done; subtasks marked `U<n> pending` are added automatically on the plan page.

| Task | What to do | For | Time |
|---|---|---|---|

## Status

- **Done:** S0.1 (repo), S1.1–S1.4 (unpacked, indexed, matched with SR1, Ghidra: `port/RE_GUIDE.md` §1–2); S1.5 (what changed, `RE_GUIDE.md` §3); S2.3, S2.5 (`FORMATS.md`); S2.1, S2.2, S2.4 waiting for your U5 checks. Phase 3: all delta specs (`port/spec/*.md`, 913/913 functions, `tools/sr2_coverage.py`).
- **Next:** v0.1.0 is published (https://github.com/kylofon/street-rod-2-sdl3/releases/tag/v0.1.0). Your playtests (User to-do) → S5.6 fix batch(es) → v0.1.x patch release. When the playtests pass, the faithful port is finished and the Enhanced repo can start (game-port-setup mode B).
- Escalation rule: a subtask that fails twice on Sonnet → new Opus session with a 5-line note
  (symptom, file, what was tried). Never carry an old transcript over.

## Model guide

| Model (app model picker) | Effort | Use for | Relative cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Haiku** | low–medium | Running and adapting existing tools, regenerating outputs, symbol merges, copying files, coverage checks, packaging, FORMATS/PLAN bookkeeping | 1× |
| **Sonnet** | medium | Default: indexers, decoders for simple/known formats, delta specs, ports of changed shell/UI/driver code, most C porting | ~3× |
| **Opus** | high | Unknowns: changed race physics/AI, renderer changes, cross-module bugs, escalations | ~5× |

Subagents inherit the session's model; wide searches go to the `scout` agent (always Haiku).

## How to run a subtask (user, every time)

1. Code tab → **New session** in `C:\Coding\StreetRod2` (never continue an old session for a new
   subtask: the old context is re-billed on every turn).
2. Pick the model from the subtask table in the model picker; set the effort.
3. Send exactly: `Do S1.1 from PLAN.md.` (with the subtask id). `CLAUDE.md` tells the agent what to read.
4. When the agent says it is done: glance at the commit (`git log -1 --stat`), do any U-check it asks

"""
mkexe.py - rebuild a WORD PC EXE from a reassembled flat binary

usage:
  1) nasm -f bin RWMAIN.ASM -o RWMAIN.BIN      (or  RW.ASM -> RW.BIN)
  2) python mkexe.py [RWMAIN|RW]               -> e.g. RWMAIN_REBUILT.EXE
  3) fc /b RWMAIN_REBUILT.EXE ..\\RWMAIN.EXE    -> should report no differences

The MZ header (incl. the relocation table) is copied verbatim from the
original EXE; only the load module is replaced.
"""
import struct, os, sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
TARGET = (sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'RWMAIN').upper()
# original EXE in parent directory_cand = [os.path.join(HERE, '..', TARGET + '.EXE')]
ORIG = next(p for p in _cand if os.path.exists(p))
BIN = os.path.join(HERE, TARGET + '.BIN')
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, TARGET + '_REBUILT.EXE')

orig = open(ORIG, 'rb').read()
bin_ = open(BIN, 'rb').read()

hdrpara = struct.unpack('<H', orig[8:10])[0]
header = bytearray(orig[:hdrpara * 16])

# Module size equals the original exactly (verified by NASM roundtrip), so the
# original MZ header — including e_crlf/e_pages, which the originals count with
# differing conventions (NLQ includes the 512-byte header in e_pages, RWMAIN
# does not) — is kept VERBATIM. Recomputing e_pages from the module alone
# under-counts by one page and DOS silently truncates the module tail at load
# (this bug made RWMAIN hang in graphics mode and RW show incomplete glyphs).
assert len(bin_) == len(orig) - hdrpara * 16, 'module size drifted!'

open(OUT, 'wb').write(bytes(header) + bin_)
print('wrote', OUT, '(header %d + module %d = %d bytes)' % (len(header), len(bin_), len(header) + len(bin_)))
if bytes(header) + bin_ == orig:
    print('IDENTICAL to original %s.EXE' % TARGET)
else:
